problemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Enable a regulated financial institution to operate a secure agency-banking channel through approved agents while preserving core banking as the authority for customer accounts and financial posting.
scope: Agent registration, verification, approval, suspension and access control.
Customer onboarding and identity verification.
Cash deposits, withdrawals, transfers and balance enquiries.
Pre-posting limits, fees, liquidity and fraud controls.
Transaction state, idempotency and timeout resolution.
Controlled reversals, settlement, reconciliation and disputes.
Receipts, notifications, immutable audit evidence and operational observability.
Provider-neutral integration with core banking, identity/KYC, payment-switch, fraud and reconciliation services.
journeys: Register and verify an agent, obtain human approval, activate permitted services and suspend access when required.
Authenticate an agent and authorize a requested operation against agent status, role and permissions.
Capture customer information, invoke identity verification and prevent onboarding completion when verification is unresolved or rejected.
Validate and submit a cash deposit or withdrawal, expose an explicit status and issue a receipt only from authoritative transaction state.
Perform a transfer or balance enquiry using governed bank interfaces.
Evaluate limits, fees, agent liquidity and fraud policy before any financial posting request.
Resolve an ambiguous timeout by retaining a pending state, querying authoritative systems and reconciling before any retry.
Initiate a controlled reversal or dispute, preserve links to the original transaction and reconcile the outcome.
Reconcile channel records against core, switch and finance records and route exceptions for controlled resolution.

qualityDrivers.statement: Remain available during dependency degradation without unsafe offline financial posting.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Agency users require predictable degraded behavior, while uncertain or unavailable dependencies must not cause unauthorized or duplicate financial postings.

qualityDrivers.statement: Protect personal and financial data using least privilege, encryption and explicit trust boundaries.
qualityDrivers.rationale: The channel processes sensitive customer, agent and transaction information across internal and external integrations.

qualityDrivers.statement: Provide end-to-end correlation, failure detection and reconciliation.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Distributed financial operations require traceable status and evidence sufficient to resolve timeouts and mismatches.

qualityDrivers.statement: Define recovery, replay, cutover and rollback controls without assuming unapproved targets.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Recovery must preserve financial correctness, and quantitative availability or recovery targets have not been supplied.

constraints: Core banking remains the system of record for customer accounts and financial posting.
Architecture changes require human approval and traceability.
The logical design must remain provider-neutral until physical technology selection.
External identity and payment-switch services may be unavailable or slow.
Unsafe offline financial posting is not permitted.
Availability, latency, throughput, RTO and RPO targets remain unconfirmed.
assumptions: Agents use managed or registered channels.
The bank can expose governed core-banking and payment-switch interfaces.
External dependencies expose sufficient correlation or query capabilities to resolve uncertain outcomes; this assumption must be validated before implementation.
Human approval workflows and accountable operational roles can be established by the bank.
ambiguities: The authoritative source and reservation semantics for agent cash liquidity or float are not identified.
The boundary between core-routed and payment-switch-routed transfers is not specified.
Customer-master ownership outside customer accounts is not explicitly stated.
Required agent authentication factors, device controls and credential lifecycle are not specified.
The status and reversal capabilities exposed by core banking and the payment switch are unknown.
Retention periods and permissible data fields for audit, receipts and operational telemetry are not defined.
unresolvedQuestions: What availability, latency, throughput, capacity, RTO and RPO targets will be approved?
Which system is authoritative for agent float, liquidity reservations and settlement balances?
Which transaction types require the payment switch, and how are switch outcomes represented in core banking?
Which authentication factors and managed-device requirements apply to agents and supervisors?
What idempotency, status-query and reversal contracts are supported by core banking and the payment switch?
Which identity-verification outcomes permit onboarding, referral or rejection?
What limits, fee schedules, fraud rules and approval authorities apply?
What data classification, retention, residency and deletion rules apply to each data set?
What constitutes an approved manual reconciliation or reversal, and which roles must be segregated?
Which deployment topology and failure domains are available?

systemContext: Retail customers transact through approved agency agents using the Agent Channel.
The Agency Banking Platform authenticates agents, orchestrates onboarding and financial requests, evaluates controls and maintains channel transaction state.
Core Banking remains authoritative for customer accounts, balances and financial postings.
The Identity/KYC Provider supplies verification results but does not independently activate customers in the agency channel.
The Fraud Platform supplies risk decisions or signals used before posting.
The Payment Switch routes applicable payment instructions; its outcome must be correlated with core-authoritative posting state.
The Reconciliation Platform and finance users compare channel, core, switch and settlement records.
Operations, support, supervisors and risk users access controlled administrative functions with auditable actions.
Notification delivery is a non-authoritative side effect and cannot determine financial success.

components.name: Agent Channel
components.description: Managed or registered user-facing channel for agency operations.
components.responsibility: Capture agent-authenticated requests, display authoritative transaction status and receipts, prevent local interpretation of timeouts as success, and avoid storing unnecessary sensitive data.

components.name: Access Gateway and Agent IAM
components.description: Channel trust boundary and enforcement point for authenticated access.
components.responsibility: Authenticate agents and administrators, validate channel or device context where approved, apply coarse-grained authorization and rate controls, and propagate trusted identity and correlation context.

components.name: Agent Lifecycle Service
components.description: Controlled system for agency-agent records and lifecycle workflow.
components.responsibility: Register, verify, route for human approval, activate and suspend agents; maintain roles, permitted operations and auditable lifecycle history.

components.name: Customer Onboarding Service
components.description: Orchestrates customer capture and identity verification.
components.responsibility: Validate onboarding input, minimize transmitted data, correlate KYC requests and results, retain verification evidence, and allow completion only under approved outcome rules.

components.name: Transaction Orchestrator
components.description: Coordinates agency financial and enquiry workflows using an explicit state machine.
components.responsibility: Accept commands, enforce idempotency, obtain policy decisions, invoke governed bank interfaces, distinguish rejection, failure and uncertain outcomes, and publish authoritative channel status without replacing core posting authority.

components.name: Policy and Fraud Control Service
components.description: Pre-posting policy decision point for financial operations.
components.responsibility: Evaluate agent permissions, transaction limits, fees, authoritative liquidity information and fraud decisions before posting; return a versioned decision and reasons suitable for audit.

components.name: Core Banking Integration
components.description: Provider-neutral anti-corruption boundary for core-banking operations.
components.responsibility: Translate governed requests and responses, preserve idempotency and correlation identifiers, query authoritative status and expose only confirmed core posting outcomes to the orchestrator.

components.name: Payment Switch Integration
components.description: Provider-neutral boundary for applicable payment routing and status queries.
components.responsibility: Submit eligible payment instructions, preserve end-to-end correlation, query uncertain outcomes and normalize switch responses without treating them as independent authority for core account posting.

components.name: Transaction Journal and State Store
components.description: Durable channel record of commands, state transitions and correlation identifiers.
components.responsibility: Atomically record idempotency keys, request fingerprints, explicit transaction state and references to core or switch outcomes; support controlled recovery and reconciliation without becoming the posting ledger.

components.name: Financial Operations and Reconciliation
components.description: Controlled workspace and workflow for reversals, settlement, disputes and mismatches.
components.responsibility: Link corrective actions to original transactions, enforce approvals and segregation of duties, invoke supported reversal operations, reconcile channel records with authoritative systems and manage exceptions to closure.

components.name: Receipt and Notification Service
components.description: Asynchronous delivery of receipts and transaction messages.
components.responsibility: Generate content from recorded authoritative status, redact sensitive fields, retry delivery independently and record delivery outcome without changing financial transaction status.

components.name: Audit Evidence Service
components.description: Tamper-evident repository for security, administrative and financial-action evidence.
components.responsibility: Capture actor, action, decision, correlation, timestamps and before-and-after references; restrict access and support integrity verification under an approved retention policy.

components.name: Operational Observability
components.description: Central correlation, metrics, logs, traces and alerting for the agency channel.
components.responsibility: Detect dependency failures, accumulating pending states, reconciliation exceptions and control failures while preventing sensitive values from entering telemetry.

interfaces.name: Agent Channel API
interfaces.contract: Versioned commands and queries carrying authenticated session context, unique request identifier, transaction idempotency key where applicable and end-to-end correlation identifier.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Reject invalid or unauthorized requests before processing. A client timeout is UNKNOWN, not failure or success; the client queries status using the original identifier and must not generate a new financial command automatically.
securityControls: Strong agent authentication under approved policy

interfaces.name: Agent Lifecycle Administration API
interfaces.contract: Role-restricted registration, verification, approval, permission and suspension commands with reason, actor and correlation data.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Lifecycle changes commit atomically with audit evidence. Failed or uncertain approval operations remain non-active until status is confirmed; suspension takes precedence over cached permissions.

interfaces.name: Customer Onboarding API
interfaces.contract: Versioned onboarding submission and status query using correlation identifiers and approved customer data fields.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Validation failure rejects the request. KYC timeout or unavailable status leaves onboarding pending and does not activate the customer; repeated submissions use the original request identity.

interfaces.name: Financial Transaction API
interfaces.contract: Deposit, withdrawal, transfer and balance-enquiry commands or queries with agent identity, account reference, amount where applicable, operation type, idempotency key and correlation identifier.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Commands return an explicit state such as RECEIVED, VALIDATING, REJECTED, SUBMITTED, PENDING_CONFIRMATION, POSTED, FAILED, REVERSAL_PENDING or REVERSED. Timeout never implies POSTED; retries with the same key and equivalent request return the existing result, while a changed payload is rejected.
securityControls: Request signing or equivalent integrity control subject to physical design

interfaces.name: KYC Verification Interface
interfaces.contract: Minimal approved identity attributes, provider-neutral verification request, correlation identifier and normalized verified, rejected, referred, pending or unavailable result.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Slow, unavailable or ambiguous provider outcomes remain pending and are queried or reconciled. The platform does not infer successful verification from transport acknowledgement.

interfaces.name: Policy and Fraud Decision Interface
interfaces.contract: Transaction context produces a versioned allow, deny or review decision, applicable fees, limit result, liquidity result and reason references.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: No financial posting occurs without all required pre-posting decisions. Missing, stale or unavailable mandatory decisions fail closed or remain pending according to an approved policy; denial is recorded as REJECTED.

interfaces.name: Transaction State Interface
interfaces.contract: Atomic creation, idempotency lookup, request fingerprint validation and append of permitted state transitions with external references.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: A command is not submitted externally unless its durable initial state and idempotency record exist. Invalid state transitions are rejected; recovery resumes from recorded state rather than replaying blindly.
securityControls: Encryption at rest and in transit

interfaces.name: Core Banking Application Interface
interfaces.contract: Provider-neutral balance, posting, status-query and supported reversal operations with stable bank transaction and idempotency references.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Only a confirmed core response or later authoritative query can produce POSTED or REVERSED channel status. Transport timeout yields PENDING_CONFIRMATION; retry is permitted only after status resolution or according to a validated core idempotency contract.

interfaces.name: Core Banking System Interface
interfaces.contract: Governed core contract for authoritative account queries, financial posting, status inquiry and approved corrective operations.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Core response semantics are normalized without changing authority. Unknown outcomes are queried and reconciled; the adapter does not synthesize success or perform unvalidated duplicate retries.

interfaces.name: Payment Routing Interface
interfaces.contract: Eligible payment instruction, idempotency or duplicate-control reference, correlation identifier, normalized routing result and status query.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Switch acknowledgement is not treated as core posting confirmation. Timeout yields an unresolved state; status query and reconciliation precede any resubmission or corrective action.

interfaces.name: Financial Operations Interface
interfaces.contract: Approved status-query, reversal or corrective instruction linked to the original transaction, case, reason, actor and authorization evidence.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Corrective commands are idempotent and never overwrite original evidence. Unsupported or uncertain reversals remain open cases pending authoritative resolution.

interfaces.name: Reconciliation Exchange
interfaces.contract: Controlled exchange of channel, core, switch and settlement references plus matched, unmatched and resolved outcomes.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Late or duplicate records are matched by stable references. Unmatched or conflicting records create exceptions and cannot automatically alter financial posting without an approved corrective workflow.

interfaces.name: Receipt and Notification Event Interface
interfaces.contract: Recorded transaction-state event containing a correlation identifier, approved receipt fields and destination reference.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Delivery is asynchronous and may retry safely. Delivery failure is recorded and alerted but cannot change POSTED, FAILED or reversal status; duplicate events must not produce conflicting receipts.

interfaces.name: Audit Evidence Interface
interfaces.contract: Structured actor, action, decision, correlation, timestamp and integrity metadata using an approved schema.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Evidence ingestion is durable and duplicate-tolerant. Failure raises an operational control event; financial processing behavior during audit-service degradation must be explicitly approved and tested rather than silently discarding evidence.

interfaces.name: Telemetry Interface
interfaces.contract: Correlated metrics, traces, sanitized logs and control events using transaction, dependency and deployment identifiers.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Telemetry loss does not imply transaction failure or success. Collection is buffered where safe, health degradation is surfaced, and sensitive transaction data is excluded.

dataArchitecture: Core Banking owns authoritative customer account, balance and financial posting records.
The Agent Lifecycle Service owns agency-agent profile, approval status, permissions and suspension history; identity evidence sources remain distinguishable from bank approval decisions.
The Customer Onboarding Service owns channel onboarding workflow and KYC correlation evidence. Final customer-master ownership must be confirmed; customer accounts remain core-owned.
The Transaction Journal owns channel command identity, request fingerprint, state history and correlation references, but is not a financial ledger and cannot override core posting state.
Agent liquidity or float authority is unresolved. The policy service must consume an approved authoritative source and must not infer liquidity from local channel observations.
Limits, fees and fraud-policy versions are controlled configuration with named owners, human-approved changes, effective dates and audit history.
The Financial Operations component owns reconciliation cases, dispute workflow and links to original transactions; core and switch records retain their respective authority.
The Audit Evidence Service stores tamper-evident evidence under an approved retention and access policy; it does not duplicate unnecessary customer secrets.
Receipts and telemetry contain only approved, minimized projections and correlation references.
All data contracts carry classification metadata, ownership, purpose, retention disposition and access rules once those policies are approved.
securityArchitecture: Treat the agent device/channel, platform edge, internal services and each external dependency as separate trust boundaries.
Authenticate human and service identities; authorize by agent status, role, operation, account context and administrative responsibility.
Apply least privilege to APIs, databases, secrets, audit access and operational tooling; separate agent, supervisor, support, finance and security capabilities.
Encrypt sensitive data in transit and at rest using bank-approved mechanisms selected during physical design.
Prevent replay and duplicate commands through authenticated sessions, unique command identities, idempotency records and request fingerprints.
Minimize KYC, receipt, audit and telemetry fields; prohibit sensitive values from unrestricted logs or traces.
Protect policy and configuration changes with versioning, human approval, traceability and rollback.
Use segregation of duties for agent approval, policy administration, reversals, reconciliation resolution and privileged access.
Manage credentials and keys through approved secret-management and rotation processes without embedding them in clients or deployment artifacts.
Record security-relevant and financial actions in tamper-evident audit evidence and monitor access to that evidence.
deploymentRuntime: Use a provider-neutral logical deployment comprising an edge trust boundary, independently deployable stateless services, durable transaction state, audit storage, event delivery and controlled integration connectors.
Distribute runtime instances across approved failure domains once the physical topology is selected; do not assume a region count or availability target.
Keep authoritative transaction state in storage that supports atomic idempotency and state transitions. Scale stateless request processing independently from durable state and external dependencies.
Isolate core, KYC, fraud, switch, reconciliation, notification and administrative traffic through explicit network and identity policies.
Use bounded queues or equivalent durable delivery for notifications, audit and reconciliation side effects; financial posting commands are not converted into unsafe offline work.
Apply configuration-as-code or equivalent governed deployment records, artifact integrity checks, environment separation and human approval for production changes.
Derive capacity, timeout, retry and circuit settings from approved targets and measured dependency behavior rather than invented defaults.
Back up and restore channel-owned durable data under approved RPO and RTO; verify that restore does not replay already posted financial commands.
resilienceFailurePaths: If agent authentication or authorization is unavailable, reject new protected operations; do not bypass controls.
If KYC is slow or unavailable, preserve onboarding as pending and allow status enquiry; do not activate based on timeout.
If fraud, limit, fee or required liquidity evaluation is unavailable, do not submit the financial posting; return rejected or pending according to approved policy.
If core banking is unavailable before submission, retain a non-posted state and permit safe status enquiry; never post locally as a substitute.
If a core request times out after submission, set PENDING_CONFIRMATION, query by stable reference, reconcile and prevent an unqualified retry.
If the payment switch times out, preserve the unresolved route status and correlate switch and core outcomes before resubmission or reversal.
If notification delivery fails, retain the financial outcome, retry delivery independently and expose delivery status to support.
If reconciliation detects a mismatch, open an exception case, freeze automated corrective action and require an approved resolution path.
If the journal cannot durably establish idempotency and initial state, do not call an external posting interface.
If audit evidence ingestion degrades, alert and follow an approved operating policy; never silently discard required evidence.
Recovery and replay resume from durable states, re-query authoritative dependencies and suppress commands already confirmed as posted.
Circuit breaking and workload isolation protect the channel from cascading dependency failure while preserving status enquiry and operational visibility where possible.
observabilityOperations: Propagate a correlation identifier from channel request through policy, core, switch, notification, audit and reconciliation records.

Monitor transaction counts by explicit state, age of unresolved states, duplicate suppression, dependency errors, policy denials, reconciliation exceptions and notification failures without assuming numeric thresholds.
Alert on growing PENDING_CONFIRMATION populations, journal write failures, unauthorized operations, audit-ingestion gaps and mismatched reconciliation records using approved thresholds.
Provide operational views that distinguish channel acceptance, external submission, core confirmation, switch status, reversal status and notification delivery.
Use structured, sanitized logs and traces; avoid customer identity documents, credentials, full account data or other unnecessary sensitive values.
Maintain runbooks for dependency outage, ambiguous timeout, duplicate request, liquidity failure, reconciliation mismatch, agent suspension, credential compromise and recovery.
Require controlled break-glass access with reason, time-bounded authorization and audit evidence.
Regularly test restore, replay suppression, dependency failover, cutover and rollback against approved targets when supplied.
transitionArchitecture: Validate core, switch, KYC, fraud and reconciliation contracts, especially idempotency, status-query and reversal behavior, before financial activation.
Resolve data ownership, agent-liquidity authority, security policy, retention and quantitative quality targets through human approval.
Implement and test agent lifecycle, identity boundary, transaction journal and audit evidence before enabling posting workflows.
Integrate enquiries and non-posting onboarding flows first to validate identity, correlation, observability and operational support.
Introduce financial operations behind controlled enablement by transaction type and agent cohort; retain a human rollback decision point.
Run reconciliation comparison and operational readiness exercises before broadening use; investigate every unexplained mismatch.
Cutover only with approved entry criteria, rollback procedures, support ownership and preserved correlation across old and new paths where an existing path is present.
Rollback disables new command intake while retaining status resolution, reconciliation and audit access for already submitted transactions; it must not erase or blindly replay in-flight work.

decisions.title: Preserve core banking as financial authority
decisions.selectedOption: Core Banking remains authoritative for customer accounts, balances and financial postings; agency records reference but do not replace core outcomes.
alternatives: Maintain an independent agency financial ledger as posting authority.
Permit offline local posting followed by later synchronization.
decisions.rationale: The scenario explicitly constrains financial posting and customer-account authority to Core Banking and prohibits unsafe offline posting.
tradeoffs: Core dependency degradation limits new financial operations.
Additional status-query and reconciliation integration is required.
consequences: Only confirmed core outcomes can produce authoritative posted or reversed status.
The channel may remain available for status, support or non-posting functions while new posting is unavailable.
Local transaction state must clearly distinguish workflow status from ledger authority.

decisions.title: Use durable idempotent transaction orchestration
decisions.selectedOption: Represent each financial request as a durable state machine keyed by a stable idempotency key and request fingerprint, with explicit uncertain states and authoritative status resolution.
alternatives: Rely on client retries and synchronous responses.
Use unrestricted at-least-once command replay.
Treat transport timeout as failure.
decisions.rationale: Distributed timeouts and retries create duplicate-posting risk unless request identity and uncertainty are durably managed.
tradeoffs: Requires durable state, transition controls and reconciliation logic.
Pending states add operational workload and user-visible uncertainty.
consequences: Equivalent retries return the existing transaction outcome.
Changed payload under an existing key is rejected.
Ambiguous external outcomes remain pending until queried or reconciled.

decisions.title: Evaluate mandatory controls before posting
decisions.selectedOption: Require successful authorization, limit, fee, authoritative liquidity and fraud decisions before submitting a financial posting.
alternatives: Evaluate selected controls after posting.
Allow posting during control-service outage and review later.
decisions.rationale: The scenario requires these policies before financial posting and identifies agent fraud and liquidity shortfall as known risks.
tradeoffs: Control dependency failure can reduce transaction availability.
Policy orchestration and versioned evidence add complexity.
consequences: Missing mandatory decisions cannot silently default to allow.
Decision versions and reasons become transaction evidence.
Control services require explicit degraded-mode procedures.

decisions.title: Separate authoritative processing from side effects
decisions.selectedOption: Complete and record authoritative financial status independently from asynchronous receipts and notifications.
alternatives: Make notification success part of transaction commit.
Allow notification providers to determine customer-visible financial status.
decisions.rationale: Notification delivery is explicitly non-authoritative and may fail independently.
tradeoffs: Users may receive delayed notifications.
Support tooling must expose separate transaction and delivery states.
consequences: Notification retries cannot duplicate financial postings.
Receipts are generated only from recorded status.
Delivery failures are operational exceptions, not posting reversals.

decisions.title: Use provider-neutral integration boundaries
decisions.selectedOption: Place normalized anti-corruption interfaces between the agency platform and core, KYC, fraud, payment-switch and reconciliation systems.
alternatives: Expose provider-specific contracts directly to channel services.
Select physical integration products during logical design.
decisions.rationale: Provider neutrality is a stated constraint and external services may be slow or unavailable.
tradeoffs: Adapters add components and translation effort.
Normalized contracts may not expose every provider-specific feature.
consequences: Provider semantics remain isolated behind owned interfaces.
Timeout, status and error normalization must preserve rather than conceal ambiguity.
Physical products remain subject to later approval.

decisions.title: Enforce explicit trust boundaries and least privilege
decisions.selectedOption: Authenticate human and service identities at each trust boundary, authorize by role and operation, encrypt sensitive data and minimize cross-boundary disclosure.
alternatives: Trust traffic based only on network location.
Use shared broad service credentials.
Replicate full customer and transaction payloads to every component.
decisions.rationale: The architecture must protect personal and financial data while supporting agents, administrators and external services.
tradeoffs: Identity lifecycle, authorization policy and key management increase operational effort.
Strict minimization can require additional purpose-specific interfaces.
consequences: Suspended agents and revoked services lose access through centrally enforced policy.
Administrative duties are separated and audited.
Telemetry and notifications use minimized projections.

decisions.title: Use reconciliation-led corrective processing
decisions.selectedOption: Resolve mismatches, disputes and uncertain outcomes through linked cases, authoritative queries and approved idempotent reversal or corrective operations.
alternatives: Delete or overwrite the original transaction.
Automatically reverse every timeout.
Resolve discrepancies outside the governed platform without correlation.
decisions.rationale: Controlled reversal, settlement, reconciliation and disputes are required, while timeout does not establish failure.
tradeoffs: Some exceptions require human review and remain open longer.
Reconciliation needs stable references across systems.
consequences: Original evidence remains immutable.
Corrective actions have separate identifiers and approval evidence.
Unsupported automated correction is blocked.

decisions.title: Defer quantitative runtime targets but require governed recovery controls
decisions.selectedOption: Define logical redundancy, backup, restore, replay suppression, cutover and rollback mechanisms now; approve numeric targets and physical topology later.
alternatives: Invent availability and recovery targets.
Omit recovery design until after deployment.
decisions.rationale: Availability, latency, throughput, RTO and RPO are explicitly unconfirmed, but recovery and rollback controls are required.
tradeoffs: Physical sizing and topology remain unresolved.
Fitness thresholds cannot be finalized until targets are approved.
consequences: No unapproved quantitative guarantee is made.
Deployment selection must demonstrate the approved targets when available.
Recovery tests must validate financial correctness as well as service restoration.

decisions.title: Retain immutable and correlated evidence
decisions.selectedOption: Capture tamper-evident audit records and durable correlation across agent lifecycle, onboarding, policy, posting, reversal, notification and reconciliation actions.
alternatives: Rely only on application diagnostic logs.
Permit mutable audit rows without integrity verification.
Store complete sensitive payloads as evidence by default.
decisions.rationale: Every financial action requires immutable audit and operational evidence, while sensitive data must be minimized.
tradeoffs: Evidence storage, integrity controls and access governance add cost and administration.
Data minimization requires carefully designed schemas.
consequences: Audit evidence is separated from ordinary diagnostics.
Retention and access policies require human approval.
Operational investigations can follow stable correlation references across systems.

risks.description: A retry or replay may cause duplicate financial posting.
risks.mitigation: Use stable idempotency keys, request fingerprints, durable state, core or switch duplicate controls, authoritative status queries and reconciliation before retry.

risks.description: An agent or compromised agent identity may perform unauthorized or fraudulent transactions.
risks.mitigation: Enforce agent approval and suspension, strong authentication, operation-level authorization, limits, fraud checks, managed-channel controls and monitored audit evidence.
risks.owner: Fraud and risk with agency operations

risks.description: Dependency timeouts may leave the financial outcome ambiguous.
risks.mitigation: Expose explicit pending status, preserve correlation, query authoritative dependencies, suppress blind retries and route unresolved cases to reconciliation.

risks.description: A cash operation may proceed despite insufficient or stale agent liquidity information.
risks.mitigation: Designate an authoritative liquidity source, use reservation semantics if supported, evaluate liquidity before posting and block processing when mandatory liquidity state is unavailable.

risks.description: Personal or financial information may be exposed through channels, integrations, receipts, logs or privileged access.
risks.mitigation: Apply explicit trust boundaries, encryption, least privilege, data minimization, redaction, controlled secrets and audited access.

risks.description: Channel, core, switch or settlement records may not reconcile.
risks.mitigation: Use stable references, complete state history, scheduled and event-driven comparison, exception cases and controlled corrective actions linked to original transactions.

risks.description: KYC, fraud, core, switch or notification dependencies may become slow or unavailable and cause cascading failure.
risks.mitigation: Use timeouts, circuit controls, workload isolation, bounded retries, explicit degraded behavior and no unsafe offline posting.

risks.description: Privileged approval, reversal, policy or reconciliation capabilities may be misused or changed without traceability.
risks.mitigation: Apply segregation of duties, fine-grained authorization, human approval, versioning, tamper-evident audit and monitored break-glass procedures.

delivery.executiveSummary: This candidate architecture introduces a provider-neutral agency-banking platform around core banking rather than a competing financial ledger. It uses authenticated agent access, controlled agent and customer onboarding, pre-posting policy evaluation, durable idempotent orchestration and explicit transaction states. Core-confirmed outcomes remain authoritative; timeouts become pending cases resolved through status queries and reconciliation, never unsafe offline posting. Notifications are asynchronous side effects. Tamper-evident audit, correlation, least privilege, controlled reversals and governed recovery are integral. Physical products, quantitative targets, liquidity authority, retention rules and detailed external contracts remain subject to human approval.

sddSections.heading: 1. Scope and Context
sddSections.content: The solution supports approved agency agents performing customer onboarding, deposits, withdrawals, transfers and balance enquiries. It integrates with core banking, identity/KYC, fraud, payment switching, reconciliation and notifications. Core banking remains authoritative for customer accounts and financial posting.

sddSections.heading: 2. Logical Architecture
sddSections.content: The logical platform contains channel access and IAM, agent lifecycle, customer onboarding, transaction orchestration, pre-posting policy controls, provider-neutral integration adapters, durable transaction state, financial operations, notifications, audit evidence and observability. Components are independently owned and communicate through versioned contracts.

sddSections.heading: 3. Transaction Processing
sddSections.content: Financial commands establish durable idempotency and initial state before external submission. Mandatory authorization, limits, fees, liquidity and fraud decisions precede posting. Confirmed core outcomes produce posted status; ambiguous outcomes remain pending and are queried or reconciled. State transitions are controlled and recoverable.

sddSections.heading: 4. Data and Authority
sddSections.content: Core owns account balances and postings. Agency services own agent lifecycle, onboarding workflow, channel transaction state, operational cases and audit evidence within their defined purposes. The transaction journal is not a ledger. Agent-liquidity and customer-master authority require confirmation.

sddSections.heading: 5. Security
sddSections.content: The design uses explicit trust boundaries, human and service authentication, fine-grained authorization, segregation of duties, encryption, replay resistance, data minimization, controlled secrets and tamper-evident audit. Physical mechanisms and authentication factors require approval.

sddSections.heading: 6. Integration and Failure Semantics
sddSections.content: Every external interface preserves correlation and distinguishes rejection, failure and uncertainty. Timeouts never imply success. Core and switch retries require validated duplicate controls or status resolution. Required policy or identity dependencies do not silently default to allow.

sddSections.heading: 7. Reversal and Reconciliation
sddSections.content: Corrective actions are separate, idempotent records linked to original transactions and approval evidence. Reconciliation compares channel, core, switch and settlement references. Conflicts create managed exceptions rather than automatic ledger changes.

sddSections.heading: 8. Deployment and Recovery
sddSections.content: The provider-neutral runtime separates edge, services, durable state, audit, events and integration connectors. Logical redundancy, backup, restore, replay suppression, cutover and rollback are required. Physical topology and numeric objectives remain open pending approval.

sddSections.heading: 9. Operations
sddSections.content: Operations receive correlated transaction and dependency status, alerts for unresolved or mismatched activity, sanitized diagnostics and runbooks for known failure paths. Break-glass activity and configuration changes are restricted and audited.

sddSections.heading: 10. Governance
sddSections.content: All architecture, policy, product, target and production changes require human approval and traceability. This package is candidate-only and makes no production acceptance claim.

openIssues: Approve availability, latency, throughput, capacity, RTO and RPO targets.
Designate the authoritative agent-liquidity or float system and its reservation semantics.
Validate core and switch idempotency, status-query, reversal and settlement contracts.
Define transaction routing boundaries between core banking and the payment switch.
Approve agent authentication factors, device-management controls and credential lifecycle.
Define KYC outcome rules and customer-master ownership.
Approve limits, fees, fraud policy, exception handling and configuration owners.
Define data classification, retention, residency, deletion and audit-access policies.
Define reversal, dispute and reconciliation approval matrices and segregation of duties.
Select physical deployment, storage, messaging, observability and security technologies through governed review.
implementationRoadmap: Phase 1: Approve unresolved ownership, security, policy, integration and quality requirements; validate dependency contracts.
Phase 2: Implement the edge trust boundary, agent lifecycle, customer onboarding, transaction journal, audit evidence and correlation foundation.
Phase 3: Implement balance enquiries and dependency status handling; exercise observability and support workflows without financial posting.
Phase 4: Implement pre-posting policy, core and switch adapters, idempotent transaction orchestration and explicit timeout resolution.
Phase 5: Implement controlled reversal, dispute, settlement and reconciliation workflows plus non-authoritative notifications.
Phase 6: Execute security, resilience, recovery, replay, reconciliation and operational-readiness tests against approved criteria.
Phase 7: Conduct a human-approved limited activation, monitor reconciliation and failure paths, then expand only through approved gates.
acceptanceAndFitnessTests: Agent lifecycle test: an unapproved or suspended agent cannot authenticate for or execute protected operations, and every approval or suspension has attributable audit evidence.
Authorization test: an authenticated agent requesting an unpermitted operation is rejected before financial processing.
KYC degradation test: a timeout or unavailable provider leaves onboarding pending and never activates the customer by inference.
Pre-posting control test: posting is not invoked when a mandatory limit, fee, liquidity or fraud decision is denied, missing or unresolved.
Idempotency test: repeated equivalent commands with the same key result in at most one external posting attempt under the validated dependency contract; a changed payload using the key is rejected.
Timeout test: loss of a posting response produces PENDING_CONFIRMATION, status enquiry and reconciliation rather than an automatic new command.
Authority test: neither channel state, switch acknowledgement nor notification delivery can independently create core-confirmed POSTED status.
Reversal test: a reversal requires authorized workflow, references the original transaction, preserves original evidence and reaches final status only from an authoritative response.
Reconciliation test: matched records close normally; missing or conflicting records create controlled exceptions without silent mutation of posting history.
Notification test: delivery failure or duplicate events do not alter financial status or produce conflicting receipts.
Audit test: each financial and privileged action can be followed by correlation identifier across policy, posting, status, notification and reconciliation evidence, with integrity checks succeeding.
Privacy test: KYC documents, credentials and unnecessary account data are absent from general logs, traces and notification payloads.
Dependency-isolation test: slow KYC, fraud, core, switch or notification dependencies do not cause uncontrolled resource exhaustion or unsafe offline posting.
Recovery test: restoration and replay resume from durable state, query authoritative systems and do not reissue already confirmed postings.
Cutover and rollback test: approved entry and exit procedures preserve in-flight status resolution, reconciliation and audit evidence and meet approved targets once supplied.

abstentions: No physical cloud, database, messaging, identity, observability or security product was selected.
No numeric availability, latency, throughput, capacity, RTO, RPO, timeout, retry or retention target was invented.
No regulatory obligation beyond the supplied scenario was asserted.
No authentication factor, cryptographic algorithm, data residency rule or retention duration was assumed.
No authoritative agent-liquidity system, customer-master owner or payment routing rule was invented.
No production approval, implementation completion or control effectiveness claim was made.
unsupportedClaimsRejected: Rejected any claim that channel acknowledgement, switch acknowledgement or notification delivery proves financial posting.
Rejected unsafe offline financial posting during core or policy dependency failure.
Rejected automatic retry after an ambiguous financial timeout without status resolution or validated idempotency.
Rejected automatic reversal solely because a response timed out.
Rejected treating diagnostic logs as sufficient immutable financial evidence.
Rejected assigning unapproved quantitative service or recovery guarantees.
Rejected provider-specific technology selection without physical-design approval.
Rejected any architecture or Design Graph mutation, approval or automatic promotion.

problemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Fulfil customer orders reliably across inventory, payment, warehouse and delivery domains while making cross-domain consistency, compensation, reconciliation and customer-visible status explicit.
scope: Order acceptance and authoritative customer-facing order status
Inventory reservation and release
Payment authorization, capture, void and refund
Fulfilment creation, hold, release and cancellation
Delivery creation and cancellation through a carrier integration
Material customer notifications
Event transport, journaling, reconciliation and operator recovery
journeys: Accept an order, reserve inventory, authorize payment, prepare fulfilment, capture payment and initiate delivery.
Cancel before capture by cancelling work, voiding authorization and releasing inventory.
Cancel after capture but before dispatch by stopping work where possible, refunding payment and releasing inventory.
Expose current order state, pending actions and recoverable failure status to customers and support.
Detect and reconcile stuck workflows, duplicate commands, missing outcomes and out-of-order events.
Notify the customer of material order-state changes without making notification delivery part of the order transaction.

qualityDrivers.statement: Define local consistency boundaries, stable idempotency keys and aggregate-scoped ordering rules.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Events may be duplicated, delayed or delivered out of order, and no cross-domain transaction is permitted.

qualityDrivers.statement: Contain partial failure through bounded retries, dead-letter handling, compensation and operator recovery.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Payment and delivery providers have independent availability, so unresolved outcomes must remain visible and recoverable.

qualityDrivers.statement: Correlate commands, events, provider calls and business state end to end.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Operators must reconstruct an order journey and distinguish missing, duplicate and delayed work.

qualityDrivers.statement: Authenticate and authorize producers, consumers and operators while minimizing exposure of sensitive order and payment data.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Domain events and recovery controls cross trust boundaries and can trigger financially consequential actions.

constraints: No distributed transaction spans payment, inventory and fulfilment systems.
Events may be duplicated, delayed or arrive out of order.
External payment and delivery providers have independent availability.
All cross-domain outcomes must therefore use eventual consistency and explicit compensation.
assumptions: Each domain can own a durable transactional store.
Business operations can define and approve compensation policies.
Each domain can persist idempotency and processing state with its business transaction.
Domain owners can expose query operations for reconciliation, even when a command outcome event is missing.
ambiguities: The business-approved point at which payment should be captured is not specified; this candidate uses fulfilment readiness as the capture trigger and prevents dispatch until capture is confirmed.
Post-dispatch cancellation, return and refund policy is not specified.
External provider support for idempotency keys, status queries and cancellation is not stated.
Notification channels and delivery expectations are not specified.
Data retention, event replay windows and operational recovery thresholds are not specified.
unresolvedQuestions: Must the payment provider support both merchant idempotency references and status lookup before production acceptance?
Which order states are customer-visible, and which state transitions require notifications?
What is the approved compensation for delivery creation failure after payment capture?
When is a shipment no longer cancellable, and what return process applies after that point?
Who approves payment refunds and high-impact event replays?
What identity mechanism, data classification, retention policy and operational objectives apply?

systemContext: Customers and customer support submit orders and read authoritative order status through the Order API.
The Order component owns the customer-facing order state and orchestrates the cross-domain saga; each downstream domain remains authoritative for its own business records.
Inventory owns reservations, Payment owns payment intents and financial-operation state, Fulfilment owns warehouse work, and Delivery owns shipment requests and carrier interaction.
Domain services publish events through an event backbone using transactional outboxes. Consumers use durable inboxes and idempotent handlers.
Reconciliation consumes the event journal, queries domain state and provides controlled replay or repair paths for operators.
External payment and carrier systems are independent failure domains; timeout or transport failure is treated as an unknown outcome until queried.

components.name: Order and Workflow Service
components.description: Owned by the Commerce product owner and operated with SRE support. It accepts orders, stores authoritative customer-facing order state and runs the cross-domain process manager.
components.responsibility: Atomically persist orders, workflow transitions and outgoing events; issue idempotent domain commands; apply only valid state transitions; expose status including pending reconciliation; initiate compensation when policy permits.

components.name: Inventory Service
components.description: Owned by Warehouse operations. It is authoritative for stock availability and inventory reservations.
components.responsibility: Create, confirm, expire and release a named reservation exactly once at the logical-operation level, using an order-derived idempotency key and a locally atomic reservation-plus-outbox transaction.

components.name: Payment Service and Provider Adapter
components.description: Owned by Finance. It is authoritative for the internal payment intent, operation ledger and observed provider outcomes.
components.responsibility: Authorize, capture, void and refund against stable operation keys; isolate provider credentials; record every attempted and observed outcome; query ambiguous provider results before repeating a consequential operation.

components.name: Fulfilment Service
components.description: Owned by Warehouse operations. It is authoritative for warehouse work and whether work remains cancellable.
components.responsibility: Create idempotent fulfilment work in a held state, report readiness, release work for dispatch only after payment capture confirmation, and apply explicit cancellation outcomes.

components.name: Delivery Service and Carrier Adapter
components.description: Owned by Warehouse operations. It is authoritative for the internal shipment request and observed carrier state.
components.responsibility: Create or cancel shipment requests idempotently, map carrier responses to domain events, and query the carrier after ambiguous outcomes rather than blindly repeating work.

components.name: Event Backbone and Journal
components.description: Owned operationally by SRE, with event schemas owned by the publishing domains. It transports durable domain events and retains the governed journal needed for replay and diagnosis.
components.responsibility: Authenticate publishers and consumers, durably transport events with at-least-once delivery semantics, isolate failed deliveries, preserve event metadata and support controlled replay without claiming global ordering or exactly-once delivery.

components.name: Reconciliation and Recovery Service
components.description: Owned by SRE for operation, with Finance, Warehouse operations and Commerce retaining approval authority over their business repairs.
components.responsibility: Detect workflows that are stale, divergent, duplicated or missing expected outcomes; compare journal and domain state; quarantine unsafe cases; and provide audited replay or compensating-command workflows.

components.name: Notification Service
components.description: Owned by the Commerce product owner. It consumes material order-state events and sends customer communications through channels selected separately.
components.responsibility: Render and send idempotent notifications, record delivery outcomes and retry independently without blocking or changing the authoritative order state.

interfaces.name: Order Command and Status API
interfaces.contract: AcceptOrder requires a client request key and order data; cancellation requires order identity and expected current version; status returns order version, lifecycle state, pending action, reconciliation flag and domain references.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Order acceptance and its outbox record commit atomically. Repetition with the same key returns the prior logical result; reuse with conflicting content is rejected. A timeout is resolved by querying by request key before resubmission.
securityControls: Authenticate customer and support identities through an approved identity mechanism.
Authorize support actions separately from customer actions.
Encrypt transport and redact sensitive fields from logs.
Audit order creation, cancellation and privileged status access.

interfaces.name: Inventory Reservation Command API
interfaces.contract: ReserveInventory and ReleaseInventory carry commandId, orderId, reservationId, operation type, correlationId and expected reservation state. Reservation ownership is Warehouse operations.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: The API acknowledges durable acceptance or returns a definitive rejection; the business outcome is published as an event. Commands are deduplicated by commandId. On timeout, the workflow queries reservationId before retrying. Terminal reservation failure prevents progression; compensation releases any confirmed reservation.
securityControls: Authorize only reservation operations for the Order workload.
Validate schema and reject conflicting idempotency-key reuse.
Encrypt transport and audit state-changing commands.

interfaces.name: Payment Lifecycle Command API
interfaces.contract: Authorize, Capture, Void and Refund carry paymentIntentId, commandId, orderId, operation generation, amount reference, correlationId and expected payment state.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Each operation key identifies one logical financial action. Duplicate commands return the recorded state. Unknown provider outcomes remain pending and are queried before retry or compensation. Capture is not treated as successful until confirmed; dispatch remains held while capture is unresolved.
securityControls: Authenticate and authorize the Order workload by operation.
Do not place payment instrument data in commands or events; use opaque provider or payment-intent references.
Encrypt transport and maintain an immutable audit trail of attempts and outcomes.

interfaces.name: Fulfilment Command API
interfaces.contract: CreateFulfilment, ReleaseToDispatch and CancelFulfilment carry fulfilmentId, orderId, commandId, correlationId and expected fulfilment state.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Creation is idempotent and initially held. ReleaseToDispatch is accepted only from a valid ready state after the Order workflow observes confirmed capture. Cancellation returns or emits Cancelled, AlreadyCompleted or CannotCancel; ambiguous outcomes are queried before further compensation.
securityControls: Authenticate and authorize the Order workload.
Encrypt transport and audit create, release and cancel actions.

interfaces.name: Delivery Command API
interfaces.contract: CreateShipment and CancelShipment carry shipmentId, fulfilmentId, orderId, commandId, correlationId and expected shipment state.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Commands are durably deduplicated. A carrier timeout creates an unknown internal state and triggers status inquiry; it does not authorize blind shipment recreation. A definitive cancellation refusal is emitted for workflow and operator handling.
securityControls: Authenticate and authorize the Fulfilment workload.
Encrypt transport and audit shipment creation and cancellation.

interfaces.name: Payment Provider Integration
interfaces.contract: Map each internal payment operation to a stable merchant operation reference and retain provider references and normalized outcomes. Provider-specific capabilities remain isolated in the adapter.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Transport failure or timeout is an unknown outcome. The adapter queries by the stable reference before repeating an operation. If the provider cannot support safe inquiry or idempotency, the case is quarantined for Finance rather than automatically repeated.
securityControls: Keep provider credentials only in the Payment boundary.
Exclude sensitive provider payloads from general events and logs.
Audit credential use and consequential operations.

interfaces.name: Carrier API Integration
interfaces.contract: Map internal shipment and cancellation operations to stable carrier request references and normalize carrier status into delivery events.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Timeout is treated as unknown; status is queried before creating another shipment. Definitive failure is published for retry, compensation or manual handling. Carrier cancellation refusal does not overwrite the internal record.
securityControls: Keep carrier credentials within the Delivery boundary.
Minimize customer delivery data sent and logged.

interfaces.name: Domain Event Publication
interfaces.source: CMP-ORDER, CMP-INVENTORY, CMP-PAYMENT, CMP-FULFILMENT and CMP-DELIVERY
interfaces.owner: SRE for transport; publishing domain for schema and meaning
interfaces.contract: Every event carries eventId, eventType, schemaVersion, aggregateId, aggregateVersion, occurredAt, correlationId, causationId, producer identity and a payload containing only necessary business data.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: The domain state and outbox record commit in one local transaction. Relay retries may produce duplicates. Delivery is at least once; there is no global ordering. An aggregateVersion gap or regression is held for reconciliation rather than applied as current state.
securityControls: Authenticate producers and authorize publication by event family.
Encrypt transport and stored journal data.
Apply schema validation and payload allowlists.
Exclude payment instruments, credentials and unnecessary customer data.

interfaces.name: Domain Event Subscription
interfaces.target: CMP-ORDER, CMP-RECON, CMP-NOTIFICATION and authorized domain consumers
interfaces.owner: SRE for subscription operation; consuming domain for processing correctness
interfaces.contract: Consumers validate schemaVersion and producer, deduplicate eventId in a durable inbox, enforce aggregateVersion rules and record processing outcome with correlation metadata.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Handler failure is retried according to operational policy and then isolated in a dead-letter path. Replay preserves eventId. Unsupported schemas or unresolved ordering gaps are quarantined; they are not silently discarded or applied out of sequence.
securityControls: Authenticate consumers and authorize subscriptions by least privilege.
Redact sensitive payload fields from diagnostics.

interfaces.name: Reconciliation Query and Recovery Interface
interfaces.target: CMP-ORDER, CMP-INVENTORY, CMP-PAYMENT, CMP-FULFILMENT and CMP-DELIVERY
interfaces.owner: SRE for tooling; relevant domain owner for repair approval
interfaces.contract: Supports correlation-based state queries, dead-letter inspection, replay with the original eventId and issuance of new compensating commands with new commandIds linked to the original causation chain.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Read-only comparison precedes repair. Replays remain idempotent. Payment retries, refunds and irreversible warehouse or delivery actions require domain-authorized workflows. Failed repair remains open and auditable rather than being marked resolved.
securityControls: Strong operator authentication and role separation.
Least-privilege read, replay, refund and compensation permissions.
Approval controls for financially or operationally consequential repairs.
Tamper-evident audit history without sensitive payload disclosure.

interfaces.name: Customer Notification Delivery
interfaces.contract: Send a template and minimal order-state data under a notificationId derived from orderId, orderVersion and notification type.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Delivery is asynchronous and idempotent per notificationId. Failures retry and then enter an operator-visible failure path. Notification failure never rolls back or changes order state.
securityControls: Send only data required by the selected channel.
Protect channel credentials and encrypt supported transport.
Prevent sensitive payment data from entering templates or logs.
Audit template version and delivery outcome.

dataArchitecture: Order is authoritative for the customer-facing order lifecycle and workflow state; it stores references to, but does not replace, authoritative domain records.
Inventory owns InventoryReservation, Payment owns PaymentIntent and its operation ledger, Fulfilment owns warehouse work, and Delivery owns Shipment.
Each domain uses a local transaction for business state, idempotency record and outbox entry. Consumers atomically persist inbox completion with their local state change.

The common event envelope includes eventId, aggregateId, aggregateVersion, correlationId, causationId, schemaVersion, producer and occurrence time. Ordering is defined only within an aggregate version sequence.
Stable command keys identify logical operations. Separate generations distinguish a legitimate later refund or retry decision from accidental redelivery of an earlier command.
The event journal supports diagnosis and replay but is not the authority for current inventory, payment, fulfilment or shipment state.
Events contain opaque payment-intent and provider references rather than payment instruments or credentials. Customer data is minimized by event type.
Schema compatibility, retention duration, deletion rules and replay windows require approved policies before production acceptance.
securityArchitecture: Use authenticated workload identities for command APIs, event publication and subscriptions; authorize each identity only for required operations and event families.
Use authenticated customer and support identities at the Order API, with separate privileges for support and operator recovery.
Encrypt service, event and provider traffic and protect durable stores and journals according to the eventual data-classification policy.
Keep payment-provider credentials and detailed provider payloads inside the Payment boundary; keep carrier credentials inside Delivery.
Apply schema validation, payload allowlists, log redaction and event-field minimization to prevent sensitive data propagation.
Audit order cancellation, payment operations, shipment operations, dead-letter release, replay and manual compensation with actor, correlation and outcome.
Separate read-only reconciliation from replay, refund and irreversible repair permissions. Require domain-owner approval for consequential recovery actions.
Rotate and revoke workload and provider credentials through an approved secret-management process; the specific mechanism is unresolved.
deploymentRuntime: Deploy domain services with independently owned durable stores so that no shared database creates an implicit cross-domain transaction.
Run an event backbone with durable subscriptions, dead-letter isolation and a governed event journal.
Run an outbox relay for every event-producing domain and durable inbox processing for every state-changing consumer.
Isolate payment-provider and carrier adapters from core domain logic so external failure does not corrupt local state.
Run reconciliation workers separately from operator controls; automated workers may detect and propose deterministic repairs, while consequential actions follow authorization policy.
Use backward-compatible event deployment and consumer-first migration for schema changes; quarantine unsupported versions rather than dropping them.
Expose health, backlog, workflow-age, provider-outcome and reconciliation signals without placing sensitive values in telemetry.
resilienceFailurePaths: If inventory reservation is rejected, the order transitions to a definitive non-fulfillable state and no payment authorization is requested.
If payment authorization fails after reservation, the workflow issues an idempotent inventory release. An unconfirmed release becomes an orphan-reservation reconciliation case.

If fulfilment creation cannot be completed after payment authorization, the workflow holds progression, then applies the approved policy to void authorization and release inventory; unresolved outcomes remain recoverable.
This candidate creates fulfilment in a held state. When fulfilment reports readiness, the workflow requests capture. Dispatch is not released until capture is confirmed.
If capture times out, Payment queries the provider using the stable operation reference. The order remains capture-pending and warehouse dispatch stays held.
If delivery creation times out, Delivery queries the carrier before retrying. Duplicate shipment creation is not used as a recovery action.
Before capture, cancellation requests cancellation of fulfilment, void of authorization and release of reservation. Each domain reports a definitive or unresolved outcome.

After capture but before dispatch, cancellation attempts to stop fulfilment and delivery, then requests refund and inventory release according to approved policy. Partial success is visible as reconciliation-required.
After dispatch, the workflow does not assume cancellation is possible; the unresolved return and refund policy requires operator handling until defined.

Outbox relay failure leaves the committed event pending for retry. Consumer failure enters retry and then a dead-letter path. Replay preserves original identity so inbox deduplication remains effective.
Aggregate-version gaps, regressions or conflicting idempotency-key reuse are quarantined. Reconciliation compares domain state and journal history before applying any repair.
Notification failure is retried and surfaced operationally but never blocks or reverses fulfilment.
observabilityOperations: Propagate orderId, workflowId, commandId, eventId, aggregateVersion, correlationId and causationId across APIs, events and provider adapters.
Record structured transition logs showing prior state, attempted transition, resulting state and reason, while excluding sensitive payment and customer values.

Monitor pending workflows by state and age, outbox backlog, consumer lag, dead-letter volume, duplicate suppression, sequence gaps, provider unknown outcomes, compensation failures and domain divergence.
Alert thresholds and recovery time objectives must be established by SRE and business owners rather than inferred from the scenario.
Provide runbooks for payment unknown outcome, orphaned inventory reservation, stuck held fulfilment, duplicate or missing event, carrier ambiguity and inconsistent cancellation.
Require operators to inspect authoritative domain state before replay. Preserve the original event identity on replay and create a new linked identity for compensating commands.
Audit manual status correction, replay, refund, void, reservation release and shipment cancellation, including approval and final outcome.
Periodically exercise reconciliation and compensation paths with non-sensitive test orders before production acceptance.
transitionArchitecture: Phase 1: Confirm domain ownership, customer-visible state model, capture point, cancellation matrix, operator approvals and provider capabilities.
Phase 2: Establish versioned command and event envelopes, idempotency rules, correlation fields, schema compatibility rules and security boundaries.
Phase 3: Implement Order acceptance and status, domain-local stores, transactional outboxes, durable inboxes and authenticated event transport.
Phase 4: Integrate Inventory and Payment, including provider ambiguity handling and reconciliation, before enabling fulfilment progression.
Phase 5: Add held Fulfilment, capture-gated dispatch, Delivery and carrier ambiguity handling; validate cancellation at every state.
Phase 6: Add Notification and operator recovery controls, then exercise duplicate, delay, out-of-order, outage and replay scenarios.
During migration, adapters may translate existing domain contracts to the governed envelope, but authoritative ownership remains with the originating domain.
Production acceptance requires closure or explicit business acceptance of the unresolved capture, post-dispatch, provider-capability, identity, retention and operational-policy issues.

decisions.title: Use an orchestrated saga with local consistency boundaries
decisions.selectedOption: The Order component persists the authoritative order workflow and coordinates domains through commands and outcome events; every domain commits only its local state.
alternatives: Pure event choreography with no central process owner
Distributed transaction across domains
Shared database and shared order transaction
decisions.rationale: A process manager makes pending work, cancellation, compensation and customer-visible status explicit while respecting the prohibition on distributed transactions.
tradeoffs: The Order workflow becomes coupled to domain outcome contracts.
Cross-domain state is eventually consistent.
The workflow state machine requires careful versioning and recovery.
consequences: Order exposes authoritative customer-facing state without claiming authority over payment, inventory or shipment records.
Every step must define forward progress, compensation and unresolved outcomes.
No component may infer cross-domain atomic completion.

decisions.title: Use idempotent command APIs with asynchronous domain outcomes
decisions.selectedOption: Submit commands through authenticated domain APIs that durably accept or reject work; publish final business outcomes as domain events.
alternatives: Publish all commands as events
Use synchronous request chains until the entire order completes
Let domains directly update Order state
decisions.rationale: This separates command ownership from eventual business completion and makes target unavailability and unknown outcomes visible.
tradeoffs: API submission is temporarily coupled to target availability.
The workflow needs retry and query logic.
Additional accepted-versus-completed states are required.
consequences: A timeout must be resolved by querying the target with the stable operation key.
Domain services remain responsible for validating and applying their own transitions.
Order progression is driven by confirmed outcome events, not transport acknowledgement.

decisions.title: Use transactional outbox and durable inbox patterns
decisions.selectedOption: Persist domain state and its outbox atomically, relay with at-least-once delivery, and atomically record consumer deduplication with resulting local state.
alternatives: Publish directly after database commit
Rely on event transport exactly-once claims
Use a cross-domain transaction coordinator
decisions.rationale: This closes the local state-versus-event publication gap without introducing a distributed transaction.
tradeoffs: Delivery duplicates remain possible.
Relays and inboxes add storage and operational complexity.
Journal retention and cleanup policies are required.
consequences: Consumers must be idempotent.
Outbox and inbox backlogs become operational signals.
Replay must retain event identity.

decisions.title: Define aggregate ordering, idempotency and correlation explicitly
decisions.selectedOption: Use unique event and command identifiers, stable logical-operation keys, aggregate versions and end-to-end correlation and causation identifiers; make no global-ordering assumption.
alternatives: Depend on arrival order
Use timestamps as the sole ordering mechanism
Attempt global serialization of all order events
decisions.rationale: The scenario explicitly permits duplication, delay and out-of-order arrival.
tradeoffs: Sequence gaps can delay processing.
Aggregate version management adds contract complexity.
Some cases require reconciliation rather than automatic application.
consequences: Duplicate events are acknowledged without repeating effects.
Stale events cannot regress current state.
Version gaps and key conflicts are quarantined and observable.

decisions.title: Protect payment operations with an internal operation ledger and provider inquiry
decisions.selectedOption: Payment records one logical authorization, capture, void or refund per stable operation key and queries ambiguous provider outcomes before repetition.
alternatives: Retry provider calls blindly after timeout
Let Order call the payment provider directly
Treat transport acknowledgement as financial completion
decisions.rationale: Duplicate charging is a known risk, while the provider is an independent availability domain.
tradeoffs: Completion can remain pending during provider outage.
Provider inquiry and idempotency capabilities must be confirmed.
Finance needs an operator path for unresolved cases.
consequences: Dispatch is blocked until capture is confirmed.
Unknown outcomes are visible rather than guessed.
If the provider lacks safe idempotency or inquiry, affected operations require quarantine and Finance review.

decisions.title: Model cancellation and reconciliation as explicit workflows
decisions.selectedOption: Define state-dependent compensation, retain unresolved states, compare authoritative domain records before repair, and gate consequential repairs by domain approval.
alternatives: Mark the order cancelled immediately and repair later without tracking
Use only automatic retries
Depend entirely on manual database correction
decisions.rationale: Cancellation can partially succeed across domains, and the scenario requires explicit reconciliation of stuck, duplicate and out-of-order events.
tradeoffs: The state model contains intermediate and reconciliation-required states.
Operators need cross-domain tooling and runbooks.
Post-dispatch behavior remains dependent on an unprovided business policy.
consequences: Customer and support status can distinguish requested, completed and partially completed cancellation.
Compensation commands are idempotent and correlated to the original workflow.
Manual database edits are not the normal recovery mechanism.

decisions.title: Apply least-privilege security and data minimization at every boundary
decisions.selectedOption: Authenticate workloads and operators, authorize by operation and event family, encrypt protected paths, minimize event data and audit consequential actions.
alternatives: Trust all internal network participants
Place full provider payloads in shared events
Give reconciliation operators unrestricted domain access
decisions.rationale: Commands, events and recovery actions can expose sensitive data or trigger financial and operational effects.
tradeoffs: Identity, authorization and audit controls add operational overhead.
Payload minimization may require consumers to query an authoritative domain.
The specific identity and secret-management mechanisms remain to be selected.
consequences: Payment instrument data and credentials do not enter general events.
Replay, refund and cancellation privileges are separable.
Security-control implementation must be verified before production acceptance.

risks.description: Duplicate commands, replay or an ambiguous provider timeout could cause more than one financial operation.
risks.mitigation: Use a Payment-owned operation ledger, stable operation keys, durable command deduplication, provider idempotency where supported, provider inquiry before repetition and Finance-controlled recovery.

risks.description: Concurrent or duplicated reservation handling could allocate inventory inconsistently.
risks.mitigation: Make Inventory the sole reservation owner; enforce local atomic availability checks, reservation identity, idempotent commands and reservation-state reconciliation.

risks.description: A reservation may remain after order, payment or fulfilment failure.
risks.mitigation: Issue state-dependent release compensation, retain reservation references in the workflow and reconcile active reservations against terminal or stale order states.

risks.description: A committed domain change may not be observed because publication or consumption fails.
risks.mitigation: Use transactional outboxes, durable transport, durable inboxes, dead-letter isolation, backlog monitoring and state-versus-journal reconciliation.

risks.description: Cancellation may complete in some domains but fail or become impossible in others.
risks.mitigation: Use an explicit cancellation state machine, state-specific compensation, definitive CannotCancel outcomes, capture-gated dispatch and operator handling for unresolved or post-dispatch cases.

risks.description: Delayed or out-of-order events could regress order state or trigger an invalid next step.
risks.mitigation: Apply aggregate versions and valid-transition checks, quarantine sequence gaps, deduplicate event IDs and reconcile against authoritative domain state.
