risks.description: Independent payment or carrier unavailability can leave an operation outcome unknown.
risks.mitigation: Persist pending operations, query by stable external reference, avoid blind retries, hold dependent work and expose unresolved cases to reconciliation.

risks.description: Sensitive order or payment data could leak through events, logs, provider adapters or operator tooling.
risks.mitigation: Minimize payloads, use opaque payment references, isolate credentials, authenticate and authorize interfaces, encrypt protected paths, redact telemetry and audit privileged access.

delivery.executiveSummary: This candidate architecture uses an Order-owned orchestrated saga, domain-local transactions, idempotent command APIs and at-least-once domain events. Order is authoritative for customer-facing lifecycle state, while Inventory, Payment, Fulfilment and Delivery retain authority for their records. Transactional outboxes, durable inboxes, aggregate versions, stable operation keys and reconciliation make duplicate, delayed, lost and ambiguous outcomes explicit. Dispatch is held until payment capture is confirmed. Production acceptance remains blocked by unresolved provider capabilities, capture and post-dispatch policies, security mechanism selection and operational policy values.

sddSections.heading: Architecture style and boundaries
sddSections.content: Use an orchestrated event-driven saga. Each domain owns its store and commits only local business state, idempotency state and outbox data. No cross-domain atomicity or global event ordering is assumed.

sddSections.heading: Order lifecycle
sddSections.content: Order accepts and versions the customer-facing lifecycle. It reserves inventory, authorizes payment, creates held fulfilment, captures when fulfilment is ready, and releases dispatch only after confirmed capture. Every transition has a pending, definitive-failure or reconciliation-required representation.

sddSections.heading: Contracts and consistency
sddSections.content: Commands use stable operation keys and expected state. Events use unique identity, aggregate version, correlation, causation and schema version. Command acknowledgement means durable acceptance, while domain events communicate business outcomes.

sddSections.heading: Failure and compensation
sddSections.content: Timeouts are unknown outcomes and trigger state inquiry before retry. Failed authorization releases inventory; failed fulfilment can void authorization and release inventory; capture failure keeps dispatch held. Cancellation uses state-dependent compensation and preserves partial completion.

sddSections.heading: Payment safety
sddSections.content: Payment owns a durable operation ledger and provider adapter. It deduplicates logical operations, isolates credentials, queries ambiguous outcomes and requires Finance handling when safe provider inquiry or idempotency is unavailable.

sddSections.heading: Reconciliation and operations
sddSections.content: Reconciliation compares workflow, event journal and authoritative domain state. Dead-letter release and replay are audited, preserve event identity and are separated from high-impact compensating commands. Operators receive runbooks and correlated diagnostic views.

sddSections.heading: Security
sddSections.content: Authenticate workloads and operators, authorize by operation and event family, encrypt protected paths, minimize event payloads, isolate provider credentials and audit consequential actions. Specific identity, secret-management and retention mechanisms remain open.

sddSections.heading: Evolution
sddSections.content: Version event and command contracts, deploy compatible consumers before publishers and quarantine unsupported schemas. Introduce integrations incrementally, validating failure and compensation paths before enabling later workflow stages.

acceptanceAndFitnessTests: Repeat AcceptOrder with the same key and identical content; verify one logical order and the same result. Reuse the key with conflicting content; verify rejection.

Deliver an older aggregate version after a newer version; verify customer-facing status does not regress and the anomaly is recorded.
Introduce an aggregate-version gap; verify processing is held or reconciled rather than silently applying an invalid transition.

Replay a captured-payment event; verify no additional capture command or provider operation is created.
Fail payment authorization after inventory reservation; verify an idempotent release is issued and an unconfirmed release becomes an operator-visible reconciliation case.
Fail fulfilment creation after authorization; verify the configured void-and-release compensation path and visible unresolved state.
Request cancellation before capture, after capture but before dispatch, and after dispatch; verify state-specific outcomes, compensation and escalation behavior.
Timeout shipment creation; verify carrier inquiry occurs before any retry and duplicate shipment creation is not used as recovery.
Interrupt outbox relays and event consumers; verify backlog visibility, retry, dead-letter isolation and audited replay with original event identity.

problemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Provide governed multi-source analytics to authorised BI and model consumers while protecting personal information and preserving lineage, jurisdictional placement and auditability.
scope: Governed batch and change-data ingestion from source-owned systems
Classification, privacy transformation, processing and data-quality controls
Regional analytical storage and governed BI/model access
Lineage, access, transformation and export audit evidence
Retention, legal hold, deletion, backup and recovery of analytical data products
journeys: A data owner registers a source contract and authorises ingestion into an eligible regional cell.
The platform validates, classifies, transforms and publishes a versioned analytical data product with lineage and quality status.
An analyst requests BI access using role, purpose and jurisdiction attributes; policy is evaluated before queries execute.
A model consumer obtains approved features through the same governed access boundary.
A steward applies retention or legal hold, and the platform records deletion or hold evidence across governed copies.
An auditor correlates source, transformation, access and export events without receiving unrestricted analytical data.
SRE restores an analytical product together with compatible lineage and policy state, or rebuilds it from source under the original controls.

qualityDrivers.statement: Classify, encrypt, mask or tokenise sensitive fields across trust boundaries.
qualityDrivers.rationale: The scenario includes direct and indirect identifiers and requires protection across ingestion, processing, storage and consumption boundaries.

qualityDrivers.statement: Enforce regional or jurisdictional data-placement constraints.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Dataset and consumer-purpose policies vary by jurisdiction, so placement and transfer must be policy-controlled.

qualityDrivers.statement: Detect data-quality, lineage and pipeline-health failures.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Consumers require trustworthy products and operators require visible failure states rather than silent publication.

qualityDrivers.statement: Recover analytical data products without losing source lineage or access policy.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Restoring data without matching metadata and policy could create ungoverned or misleading products.

Jurisdiction policies vary by dataset and consumer purpose.
Analytical stores are not systems of record for operational source data.
assumptions: Source owners expose change or extract contracts.
A governed identity platform provides workforce attributes.
Source systems remain authoritative and can support agreed replay or re-extraction where their contracts permit it.
Policy owners will supply dataset classifications, permitted purposes, placement rules, retention schedules and legal-hold authority before production use.

The controlled purpose taxonomy and approval workflow are not specified.
Retention periods, deletion deadlines and legal-hold precedence rules are not specified.
Recovery objectives and acceptable source replay windows are not specified.

The boundary between query results and regulated exports is not specified.

Who approves consumer purposes, exceptional access and cross-jurisdiction transfers?

systemContext: Source systems remain authoritative and provide owned batch or change contracts to the ingestion plane.
The platform is divided into regional data cells containing ingestion, processing, analytical storage and consumption enforcement; policy determines the eligible cell.
The catalog and governance control plane holds classifications, ownership, product versions, lineage and policy references, subject to the same placement rules as data.
The governed identity platform supplies authenticated workforce and service attributes; the platform does not derive missing purpose or jurisdiction entitlements.
BI and model platforms consume data only through governed access interfaces rather than direct unmanaged store credentials.
Auditors use a restricted evidence interface over access, transformation, export and lifecycle records.
Trust boundaries exist at source ingestion, regional-cell entry, processing-to-publication, analytical-store access, consumer result delivery and administrative access.

components.name: Source Contract and Ingestion Service
components.description: Regional ingestion plane for source-owned batch and change feeds.
components.responsibility: Validate source identity, ownership, schema and placement eligibility; ingest idempotently where supported; quarantine invalid inputs; and record source checkpoints without becoming the operational system of record.

components.name: Governance Catalog and Policy Registry
components.description: Governed metadata control plane for ownership, classification, purpose, placement, lineage and product versions.
components.responsibility: Maintain versioned governance metadata and expose policy inputs and lineage queries while applying placement and access controls to sensitive metadata.

components.name: Processing and Data Quality Service
components.description: Regional orchestration and transformation plane.
components.responsibility: Execute versioned transformations, validate quality rules, isolate failed outputs and emit reproducible input-to-output lineage before publication.

components.name: Regional Governed Analytical Store
components.description: Policy-segmented analytical storage for validated products and derived features.
components.responsibility: Store approved analytical copies in eligible jurisdictions, separate unpublished from published products, enforce governed access paths and retain product-version references.

components.name: Consumption Policy Gateway
components.description: Common policy-enforcement boundary for BI queries, model feature access and governed exports.
components.responsibility: Authenticate consumers, evaluate role, purpose, dataset, classification and jurisdiction attributes, apply result controls, issue time-bounded access and record decisions and exports.

components.name: Privacy Transformation Service
components.description: Regional service for masking, tokenisation, suppression or approved de-tokenisation.
components.responsibility: Apply field-level privacy transformations according to classification and purpose, isolate token mappings and keys by eligible region, and audit privileged operations.

components.name: Audit Evidence Service
components.description: Access-controlled evidence repository and query service.
components.responsibility: Collect append-oriented events for ingestion, transformation, policy decisions, administrative activity, access, export, hold and deletion; detect gaps; and provide restricted auditor views.

components.name: Retention, Hold and Deletion Orchestrator
components.description: Lifecycle control plane for governed analytical copies.
components.responsibility: Calculate lifecycle actions from approved schedules, give legal holds precedence, propagate deletion to derived products and eligible copies, and retain outcome or exception evidence.

components.name: Platform Observability and Data Reliability Service
components.description: Operational monitoring for pipelines, lineage, quality, policy and audit delivery.
components.responsibility: Correlate health signals, detect missing lineage or audit events, block or withdraw unhealthy publications where configured, and route actionable alerts to accountable owners.

components.name: Recovery and Rebuild Service
components.description: Regional backup, restore and source-replay coordination.
components.responsibility: Capture and validate compatible data, lineage and policy recovery sets; restore them into an isolated state; or rebuild from authoritative sources before controlled republishing.

interfaces.name: Owned Source Extract or Change Feed
interfaces.contract: Versioned source identity, owner, schema, extraction or change semantics, checkpoint fields, classification hints and eligible destination region.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Delivery may be retried from the last accepted checkpoint. Duplicate-capable feeds require idempotent ingestion. Schema, ownership or placement failures are quarantined and are not published downstream.

interfaces.name: Source Registration and Classification Metadata
interfaces.contract: Registers source owner, schema version, classifications, regional eligibility, ingestion checkpoint and source-to-raw lineage reference.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Metadata registration must succeed before a feed is eligible for processing. Conflicts or unavailable policy metadata leave the data quarantined and trigger an operational alert.

interfaces.name: Validated Ingestion Handoff
interfaces.contract: Provides immutable input-version references, source checkpoints, schema version, classification and processing eligibility.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Processing consumes only committed input versions. Failed or partial processing does not advance publication state and can be retried against the same input version.

interfaces.name: Lineage and Quality Registration
interfaces.contract: Records transformation version, input and output versions, quality results, execution identity and publication eligibility.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: An output cannot become published until required lineage and quality records are committed. Registration failure leaves the output unpublished and retryable.

interfaces.name: Governed Product Publication
interfaces.contract: Publishes a versioned product with classification, eligible region, quality status, lineage reference, retention class and access-policy reference.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Publication is atomic at the product-version level. Incomplete writes remain unpublished; a policy or placement mismatch fails closed and raises an alert.
securityControls: Write access separated from consumer access

interfaces.name: Identity Attribute Exchange
interfaces.contract: Supplies authenticated subject or workload identity, role and governed workforce attributes needed for policy evaluation.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Missing, stale or unverifiable attributes cause denial rather than inferred entitlement. Identity-provider failure prevents new access decisions; existing access follows its explicit expiry and revocation rules.

interfaces.name: BI Query Access
interfaces.contract: Carries consumer identity, approved purpose, requested product and query; returns only policy-filtered, masked or aggregated results.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Policy uncertainty, unavailable classification or regional mismatch fails closed. Interrupted queries return no success record; completed result delivery and exports are auditable.
securityControls: Row, column and result controls as policy requires

interfaces.name: Model Feature Access
interfaces.contract: Requests versioned features using workload identity, model-consumer purpose, product version and eligible execution region.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Unapproved purpose, product version, region or identity is denied. Partial retrieval is not represented as a complete feature set; access and export outcomes are recorded.

interfaces.name: Policy and Catalog Decision Lookup
interfaces.contract: Retrieves the applicable classification, ownership, purpose, placement, result-control and lifecycle references for a product version.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Unknown, conflicting or unavailable policy causes access denial. Cached policy, if permitted, remains version-bound and cannot outlive its explicit validity or revocation constraints.

interfaces.name: Privacy Transformation Request
interfaces.contract: Requests a named transformation for classified fields under a dataset, purpose, consumer and regional policy context.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Unsupported or unauthorised transformations fail closed. Token operations are deterministic only where approved; mapping or key unavailability prevents publication or result release rather than exposing clear values.
securityControls: Privileged-operation approval where required by policy
No sensitive values in operational logs

interfaces.name: Audit Event Submission
interfaces.contract: Submits correlated events containing actor or workload, action, product version, policy and lineage references, outcome, region and event time without unnecessary sensitive payloads.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Events are append-oriented and deduplicated by event identity. Delivery gaps are alerted; configured sensitive operations fail closed or enter a restricted state when required audit delivery cannot be established.
securityControls: Separation of evidence writers and readers

interfaces.name: Lifecycle Command and Evidence
interfaces.contract: Issues version-bound retain, hold, release or delete commands and receives per-copy outcomes, exceptions and derived-product references.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Legal hold blocks conflicting deletion. Commands are idempotent and tracked to terminal success or explicit exception; partial deletion remains open and visible rather than reported as complete.
securityControls: Separation of hold and routine deletion permissions

interfaces.name: Reliability Telemetry
interfaces.contract: Emits pipeline state, freshness indicators, quality outcomes, lineage completeness, audit-delivery health and policy-decision failures using product and run identifiers.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Telemetry loss creates an explicit unknown-health state and alert. Missing mandatory quality or lineage signals prevent or withdraw publication according to product policy.

interfaces.name: Backup and Recovery Set
interfaces.contract: Captures region-bound analytical product versions, lineage snapshots, policy references and restoration manifests as a compatible recovery set.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: An incomplete or incompatible set is rejected. Restore occurs in isolation and remains unavailable to consumers until integrity, lineage, policy and placement checks pass.

interfaces.name: Controlled Store Query
interfaces.contract: Executes a policy-bound query or feature retrieval against an eligible published product version and returns results only to the requesting gateway context.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Direct consumer access is denied. Missing publication, policy-version mismatch or regional mismatch fails closed; interrupted execution does not create a successful access or export outcome.

dataArchitecture: Maintain distinct states for quarantined input, validated input, unpublished output and published analytical products; only published versions are consumer-visible.

Represent every product version with source owner, source checkpoint, schema, classification, jurisdiction eligibility, transformation version, quality result, lineage reference, access-policy reference and retention class.
Classify direct identifiers, indirect identifiers, operational facts, reference data, derived features, lineage and audit data independently because metadata and combinations can also be sensitive.

Propagate classification and placement labels through transformations; derived products receive at least the restrictions required by their contributing inputs unless an approved policy determines otherwise.
Keep token mappings, cryptographic material and clear identifiers outside general analytical access and within their eligible regional boundary.
Treat source systems as authoritative. Analytical corrections create a new derived version or trigger source-owner reconciliation; they do not silently overwrite operational truth.
Track derived-product dependencies so retention, legal hold and deletion can propagate to materialised outputs, exports and recoverable copies.
Bind restored data to compatible lineage and policy versions before republishing.
securityArchitecture: Use deny-by-default, role- and attribute-based authorisation with subject or workload, approved purpose, dataset, classification, jurisdiction, product version and action as policy inputs.
Issue time-bounded consumer access through C05; prohibit unmanaged BI or model credentials against C04.
Encrypt sensitive data in transit, at rest and in eligible backups; isolate keys and token mappings according to jurisdiction policy.
Apply masking, tokenisation, aggregation or suppression at ingestion, processing or result release according to the approved use case; do not infer that pseudonymised data is non-sensitive.
Separate source administration, policy administration, data processing, lifecycle control, audit reading and recovery privileges.
Require explicit, audited authority for de-tokenisation, exceptional exports, policy changes, legal holds and recovery publication.
Minimise sensitive values in logs, lineage and audit events while preserving identifiers needed to correlate evidence.
Treat administrative, metadata, consumer and regional boundaries as trust boundaries and authenticate every crossing.
deploymentRuntime: Deploy jurisdiction-aligned regional cells containing C01, C03, C04, C05 and eligible C06 capabilities.

Place C02, C07, C08, C09 and C10 regionally or partition them by jurisdiction where metadata, evidence, keys or backups are placement-restricted; the final topology depends on the unresolved residency matrix.
Route ingestion and consumption to an eligible cell before data transfer; reject rather than automatically reroute prohibited data across regions.
Use separate runtime identities and access domains for ingestion, processing, consumption, audit, lifecycle and recovery.
Keep unpublished and recovery-isolation environments inaccessible to BI and model consumers.
Promote configuration, transformations, quality rules and policy references as versioned artifacts through controlled environments; production acceptance remains outside this candidate package.
resilienceFailurePaths: Source schema, ownership or checkpoint failure: quarantine the feed, retain the last accepted checkpoint, alert the data owner and do not publish affected versions.
Classification or placement policy unavailable: fail ingestion, publication or access closed; do not infer a default region or lower classification.
Transformation or quality failure: isolate the output, preserve the input and run identifiers, record failure lineage and keep the prior valid product version distinguishable from the failed version.
Lineage registration failure: block publication because an untraceable output is not an eligible analytical product.
Identity or policy-evaluation failure: deny new access and record the failure without granting fallback privileges.
Privacy transformation or key failure: withhold affected fields or the complete result as policy dictates; never fall back to clear values.
Audit delivery failure: retry idempotently, expose an evidence-gap alert and restrict configured sensitive operations until auditable delivery is restored.
Partial deletion: retain an open deletion manifest with per-copy exceptions; never claim defensible completion while derived products or eligible backups remain unresolved.
Regional-cell loss: restore a compatible regional recovery set or replay from authoritative sources; validate placement, lineage, quality and policy before republishing.
Recovery metadata mismatch: keep restored data isolated and unavailable until a compatible policy and lineage state is restored or the product is rebuilt.
observabilityOperations: Monitor source checkpoint progress, schema drift, pipeline state, data freshness indicators, quality outcomes and publication state by product version.
Continuously reconcile published products against required lineage, classification, policy and audit-event references.
Alert accountable data owners and stewards for source or quality faults, Security for identity and audit faults, Privacy for policy conflicts, and SRE for runtime or recovery faults.
Provide restricted dashboards for regional placement, privileged access, export activity, legal holds, deletion exceptions and recovery validation.
Run periodic access reviews, purpose-entitlement reviews and unused-privilege removal under Security and data-owner accountability.
Test source replay, isolated restore, lineage-policy compatibility and controlled republishing; recovery objectives must be set by product owners before acceptance.
Protect operational logs from sensitive payloads and audit access to observability data.
transitionArchitecture: Inventory datasets, source owners, identifiers, jurisdictions, consumers, purposes, retention schedules and existing direct store access.
Define the classification taxonomy, purpose vocabulary, residency matrix, export rules and accountable policy owners before onboarding sensitive products.
Establish regional cells, identity integration, catalog metadata, audit collection and governed gateway as foundational controls.
Pilot one source-to-product path with quarantine, lineage, quality, privacy transformation, BI access, model access and evidence collection.
Migrate consumers from direct credentials to C05, then revoke unmanaged analytical-store access after validation.
Enable lifecycle propagation, legal hold, deletion manifests and recovery sets before declaring a product fully governed.
Onboard additional datasets by risk and jurisdiction, preserving source ownership and product-specific acceptance evidence.

decisions.title: Use jurisdiction-aligned regional data cells
decisions.selectedOption: Place ingestion, processing, analytical storage and consumption enforcement in regional cells selected by dataset and consumer-purpose policy.
alternatives: Single global analytical platform
Central storage with regional presentation layers
Per-source isolated platforms
decisions.rationale: Regional cells make data placement and cross-region trust boundaries explicit without assuming one global policy fits all datasets.
tradeoffs: Duplicates platform capabilities across regions.
Requires routing and policy consistency across cells.
Reduces accidental cross-region movement but does not resolve the missing residency matrix.
consequences: Every feed and request requires an eligible-region decision.
Metadata, audit, keys and backups must also be assessed for placement.
Cross-region transfers remain denied until explicitly allowed by policy.

decisions.title: Use versioned analytical product states and preserve source authority
decisions.selectedOption: Separate quarantined, validated, unpublished and published states and treat each analytical output as a version derived from an authoritative source checkpoint.
alternatives: Overwrite mutable analytical tables in place
Treat the analytical store as an operational master
Publish processing outputs before metadata completion
decisions.rationale: Versioned state supports reproducibility, controlled publication and recovery while respecting that analytical stores are not systems of record.
tradeoffs: Consumes additional storage and metadata.
Requires explicit version lifecycle management.
Corrections may require source reconciliation or full rebuild.
consequences: Consumers select or are routed to published versions only.
Operational source corrections are not made solely in analytics.
Recovery may use either a compatible recovery set or source replay.

decisions.title: Centralise consumption policy enforcement
decisions.selectedOption: Require BI and model access through a common gateway using role, purpose, classification, jurisdiction, product version and action attributes.
alternatives: Direct store grants managed separately for each consumer
Role-only access control
Independent BI and model authorisation stacks
decisions.rationale: A common enforcement point provides consistent purpose-bound decisions, privacy controls and evidence across both consumer classes.
tradeoffs: Creates a critical dependency for analytical access.
Requires a governed purpose taxonomy and reliable identity attributes.
Complex policies require careful testing and change control.
consequences: Direct unmanaged store credentials are removed.
Missing or conflicting policy fails closed.
Exceptional access and exports require explicit policy and audit treatment.

decisions.title: Make lineage and quality prerequisites for publication
decisions.selectedOption: Register source checkpoints, transformation versions, output versions and quality results before a product becomes published.
alternatives: Capture lineage asynchronously after publication
Document lineage manually
Track only pipeline-level lineage
decisions.rationale: Publication gating prevents known untraceable or failed outputs from being presented as governed products.
tradeoffs: Catalog availability enters the publication path.
Metadata defects can delay otherwise completed processing.
Transformation tooling must emit consistent lineage identities.
consequences: Lineage registration failures leave output unpublished.
Quality and lineage completeness become operationally monitored states.
Reprocessing can cite the exact prior input and transformation versions.

decisions.title: Orchestrate retention, legal hold and deletion by product dependency
decisions.selectedOption: Use lifecycle manifests that evaluate approved schedules, give legal holds precedence and track deletion across published, derived and recoverable analytical copies.
alternatives: Delete only primary analytical tables
Rely on source-system retention alone
Use manual deletion tickets without dependency tracking
decisions.rationale: Defensible lifecycle outcomes require evidence for every governed copy and explicit exceptions rather than a single best-effort delete action.
tradeoffs: Dependency and backup inventories must remain accurate.
Held and non-held data may require separable storage design.
Completion depends on policy schedules that are not yet supplied.
consequences: Deletion is not reported complete while a governed copy remains unresolved.
Legal-hold operations are separately authorised and audited.
Backup expiry or other approved handling must be included in each deletion manifest.

decisions.title: Recover data, lineage and policy as a compatible set
decisions.selectedOption: Restore region-bound recovery sets into isolation or rebuild from source, then validate data integrity, lineage, quality, placement and policy before republishing.
alternatives: Restore analytical data alone
Depend exclusively on source replay
Keep the analytical store continuously writable during recovery
decisions.rationale: A data-only restore could expose products with missing provenance or obsolete access policy.
tradeoffs: Recovery sets are more complex than data-only backups.
Source replay depends on source contracts and retained history.
Recovery time cannot be established until product objectives are supplied.
consequences: Restored data remains unavailable until governance checks pass.
Recovery tests include metadata and policy compatibility.
Analytical recovery does not make the platform the operational system of record.

decisions.title: Collect correlated, append-oriented audit evidence
decisions.selectedOption: Capture ingestion, transformation, policy, access, export, lifecycle, privileged and recovery events using shared correlation and product-version identifiers.
alternatives: Rely on infrastructure logs only
Maintain separate uncorrelated consumer logs
Audit only successful data access
decisions.rationale: Correlated events are needed to reconstruct access and transformation paths and expose evidence gaps.
tradeoffs: Audit metadata can itself be sensitive and placement-restricted.
Sensitive operations may be unavailable when required evidence delivery fails.
Event schemas and identity correlation require governance.
consequences: Evidence writers and readers are separated.
Audit payloads exclude unnecessary sensitive values.
Gaps, denied actions and failed exports are retained as evidence states.

decisions.title: Use owner-approved, versioned ingestion contracts
decisions.selectedOption: Require each source feed to declare ownership, schema, checkpoint semantics, classification hints and eligible destination before ingestion.
alternatives: Infer schemas and ownership at runtime
Accept unmanaged file drops
Use one platform-owned contract for all sources
decisions.rationale: Explicit source contracts preserve ownership and allow deterministic handling of change, duplicates and schema drift.
tradeoffs: Onboarding requires source-owner participation.
Contract changes can pause ingestion until reviewed.
Some sources may not support replay or stable change identifiers.
consequences: Unowned or incompatible feeds are quarantined.
Checkpoint and replay capability are recorded per source.
Source contract limitations become product recovery risks.

risks.description: Direct or indirect identifiers, combinations of fields, derived features or privileged de-tokenisation could enable re-identification.
risks.mitigation: Classify identifiers and combinations, minimise fields, use purpose-specific masking or tokenisation, isolate mappings and keys, review exports and audit privileged operations.

risks.description: Data, metadata, audit evidence, keys or backups could be placed in or transferred through an ineligible jurisdiction.
risks.mitigation: Use regional cells, policy-based routing, region-scoped identities and keys, deny unknown placement, inventory all copy types and test prohibited-transfer paths.

risks.description: Role changes, stale purpose attributes, exceptional grants or direct store credentials could cause privilege creep.
risks.mitigation: Use time-bounded gateway access, fail closed on stale attributes, remove direct credentials, review entitlements and audit policy changes and exceptions.

risks.description: Missing or inconsistent lineage, metadata or audit correlation could make products irreproducible and recovery unverifiable.
risks.mitigation: Gate publication on lineage, use immutable version references, reconcile metadata and events, detect gaps and restore compatible data-lineage-policy sets.

risks.description: Schema drift, failed pipelines or stale and poor-quality data could reach BI or model consumers.
risks.mitigation: Validate contracts, quarantine failures, publish only quality-approved versions, monitor freshness and quality indicators and clearly distinguish prior valid from failed versions.

risks.description: Deletion could be incomplete across derived products, exports, backups or held records, producing unsupported completion claims.
risks.mitigation: Maintain dependency and copy inventories, use idempotent manifests, give holds precedence, record per-copy outcomes and retain open exceptions until resolved.

risks.description: Source contracts may not provide sufficient history, stable checkpoints or replay capability for deterministic ingestion and recovery.
risks.mitigation: Assess each source during onboarding, record replay limits, retain eligible recovery sets and define product-specific recovery plans with the source owner.

risks.description: Audit-service failure or unauthorised evidence access could create evidence gaps or expose sensitive activity metadata.
risks.mitigation: Use authenticated append-oriented delivery, event deduplication, gap detection, restricted auditor views, regional placement and fail-closed handling for configured sensitive operations.

delivery.executiveSummary: This candidate architecture uses jurisdiction-aligned data cells, owner-approved ingestion contracts, versioned analytical products, publication-gated lineage and quality, and a common policy gateway for BI and model consumption. Sensitive fields are classified and transformed according to purpose and jurisdiction; direct store access is excluded. Lifecycle manifests coordinate retention, legal hold and deletion, while recovery restores or rebuilds data together with compatible lineage and policy. Production acceptance remains false because jurisdiction rules, purpose taxonomy, retention schedules, export rules and recovery objectives are unresolved.

sddSections.heading: Scope and Context
sddSections.content: The platform governs analytical copies from source-owned systems through ingestion, transformation, regional storage and BI or model consumption. Source systems remain authoritative.

sddSections.heading: Trust Boundaries
sddSections.content: Controls apply at source ingestion, regional-cell entry, processing publication, analytical-store access, result delivery, metadata and audit access, privacy transformation and administration.

sddSections.heading: Access Model
sddSections.content: C05 enforces deny-by-default role and attribute policies using identity, purpose, product, classification, jurisdiction and action. BI and model platforms receive no unmanaged store credentials.

sddSections.heading: Privacy and Residency
sddSections.content: Classification propagates through lineage. Masking, tokenisation, aggregation or suppression is selected by approved policy. Regional cells, keys, metadata, backups and evidence are subject to the unresolved placement matrix.

sddSections.heading: Lineage and Quality
sddSections.content: Versioned source checkpoints, transformations, outputs and quality results must be registered before publication. Missing lineage or mandatory quality evidence keeps outputs unpublished.

sddSections.heading: Lifecycle and Recovery
sddSections.content: Lifecycle manifests track holds and deletion across dependencies and recoverable copies. Recovery uses compatible data-lineage-policy sets or source replay and requires isolated validation before republishing.

sddSections.heading: Security and Audit
sddSections.content: Authenticated service identities, encryption, least privilege, privilege separation and append-oriented correlated evidence cover ingestion, transformation, policy, access, export, lifecycle and recovery.

sddSections.heading: Operations
sddSections.content: Operational controls detect pipeline, quality, freshness, lineage, policy and audit failures, with explicit unknown-health states and accountable routing.

Controlled expansion: onboard additional products by jurisdiction and sensitivity, collecting product-specific acceptance evidence before any production approval.
acceptanceAndFitnessTests: Submit an unowned or schema-incompatible source feed; verify quarantine, no downstream publication and an accountable alert.
Replay duplicate source events from an accepted checkpoint; verify no unintended duplicate published records where the source contract supports stable identities.

Re-run a transformation version against the same immutable input version; verify the output cites the same source checkpoint and complete lineage, subject to explicitly identified nondeterministic inputs.
Remove mandatory lineage or quality evidence; verify the output cannot become published.
Request BI and model access with an approved role but absent or unapproved purpose; verify denial and correlated audit evidence.
Request access from an ineligible region and attempt cross-region transfer; verify denial without automatic rerouting.
Exercise configured masking or tokenisation and then simulate transformation-key unavailability; verify clear values are never used as fallback.
Attempt direct consumer access to C04; verify denial and no unmanaged consumer credential path.
Apply a legal hold followed by a conflicting deletion command; verify deletion is blocked and both actions are evidenced.
Delete a product with derived copies or a recoverable copy still outstanding; verify the manifest remains incomplete and reports the exception.

Perform query, feature retrieval, export, privileged privacy operation and denied access; verify correlated evidence records actor or workload, purpose, product version, policy reference, region and outcome without unnecessary sensitive payloads.
Restore a recovery set with mismatched policy or missing lineage; verify isolation and no consumer publication.
Restore a compatible set or rebuild from source; verify lineage, quality, classification, placement and access policy before controlled republishing.
Attempt to modify operational truth solely in the analytical store; verify the change cannot be represented as an authoritative source correction.

No production approval, repository mutation, promotion or accepted architecture status was assigned.
unsupportedClaimsRejected: A single global region is acceptable for all datasets and metadata.
Role-only access is sufficient to satisfy purpose-bound access.
Analytical backups may ignore legal holds or residency constraints.
Restoring data without lineage and policy is an acceptable recovery.

Audit logging alone proves complete or defensible deletion.
The analytical store can become the operational system of record.

problemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Modernise the legacy core-banking estate through governed coexistence and dependency-aware migration waves while preserving customer access, financial integrity, regulatory reporting, operational control and reversible transition states.
scope: Coexistence of legacy and target cores
Channel, payment, product, general-ledger and regulatory-reporting integration
Account- and dependency-cohort migration control
Data migration and reconciliation
Batch and end-of-day transition
Cutover, rollback and exception handling
Cross-estate security, auditability, observability and operations
journeys: A channel request is authenticated, resolved to an account or product, routed according to governed migration state, and processed by exactly one authoritative core.
A payment is accepted through the authoritative core, submitted to payment rails with an idempotent identity, and reconciled with account and ledger outcomes.
A migration cohort is assessed, copied, validated, quiesced, activated on the target core, observed and either accepted or moved through a governed recovery path.
Product transactions generate controlled general-ledger postings and regulatory-reporting inputs regardless of which core is authoritative.
Batch and end-of-day workloads execute under dependency-aware orchestration with checkpoints, reconciliation and operator-controlled recovery.
Operations investigate customer, technical or financial exceptions using correlated audit, routing, transaction and reconciliation evidence.

qualityDrivers.statement: Minimise customer disruption and define measurable transition service levels.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Migration introduces routing, cutover and recovery failure modes that can affect channel access and transaction completion.

qualityDrivers.statement: Preserve security, auditability and segregation of duties across coexistence.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Two cores and a migration control plane increase privilege, control and evidence boundaries.

qualityDrivers.statement: Contain operational and data-integrity risk with rehearsed recovery paths.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Dual posting, divergence, failed cutover and batch overrun are identified scenario risks.

qualityDrivers.statement: Observe business reconciliation and technical health across both estates.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Technical availability alone cannot establish balance, posting or reporting correctness.

constraints: The legacy core cannot be replaced in a single big-bang event.
Regulatory and general-ledger obligations remain authoritative throughout transition.
Legacy interfaces and batch windows have incomplete documentation.
Customer and account migration ordering is constrained by product dependencies.
assumptions: A migration control plane can hold account-level migration state.
Parallel reconciliation can compare legacy and target outcomes.
ambiguities: The authoritative source for customer data, account data and product configuration is not identified for each transition state.
Target-core capability coverage and compatibility with existing products, payments, ledger and reporting contracts are unspecified.
Required transition service-level indicators and approved thresholds are unspecified.
The point after which a transaction or payment makes rollback unsafe is unspecified.
Legacy interface semantics, batch dependencies, data volumes and processing windows are incompletely documented.
Regulatory-reporting obligations, reporting calendars and acceptance criteria are not detailed.
The required consistency model between migration state, routing decisions and in-flight transactions is not explicitly stated.
unresolvedQuestions: Which system owns customer, account, product, balance and transaction records in every coexistence state?
What dependency rules determine a safe migration cohort?
Which target-core capabilities are ready, and which require temporary legacy processing?
What service-level indicators and thresholds must be approved for normal operation, migration windows and recovery?
Which payment and ledger actions are irreversible, and how are compensating actions authorised?
What are the actual batch dependency graph, cut-off times, restart points and downstream consumers?
What reconciliation tolerances are permitted for balances, transactions, postings and regulatory outputs?
Who may approve state transitions, cutover, rollback, reconciliation exceptions and risk acceptance?

systemContext: Channels consume stable customer, account, payment and product capabilities through an access facade rather than selecting a core directly.
A coexistence router consults authoritative, versioned migration state and sends each governed scope to either the legacy core or target core.
Legacy and target adapters isolate core-specific protocols and provide normalized outcomes, correlation identifiers and idempotency handling.
Payments, the general ledger and regulatory reporting remain explicit external control boundaries with reconciliation and audit evidence.
Migration, cutover, batch, reconciliation, security and observability services govern the transition without becoming systems of record for banking balances or ledger truth.
Operators use controlled workflows; no migration state change, cutover, rollback or exception approval is performed through an unaudited operational shortcut.

components.name: Channel Access Facade
components.description: Stable entry point for customer, account, payment and product capabilities during coexistence.
components.responsibility: Authenticate and validate requests, preserve channel contracts, assign correlation and idempotency identifiers, and pass requests to coexistence routing without exposing core location.

components.name: Coexistence Router
components.description: Policy-enforced routing layer between stable service contracts and legacy or target processing.
components.responsibility: Resolve governed scope, read a consistent migration-state version, reject ambiguous states, and route a request to one authoritative core while recording the decision.

components.name: Migration Control Plane and State Registry
components.description: Authoritative registry and workflow engine for governed migration state.
components.responsibility: Maintain versioned account- or cohort-level state, dependency references, transition prerequisites, approvals, audit history and controlled state changes.

components.name: Legacy Core Adapter
components.description: Anti-corruption boundary for legacy online and batch interfaces.
components.responsibility: Translate normalized contracts to documented legacy behavior, preserve legacy identifiers, enforce idempotency where supported, and expose explicit timeout and uncertain-outcome states.

components.name: Target Core Adapter
components.description: Boundary exposing target-core capabilities through the same normalized coexistence contracts.
components.responsibility: Translate requests and outcomes, enforce identifiers and idempotency controls, and expose target processing, health and batch status for routing and reconciliation.

components.name: Payment Integration Service
components.description: Controlled boundary between authoritative core processing and payment rails.
components.responsibility: Correlate payment instructions and outcomes, prevent unintended resubmission, manage uncertain outcomes, and provide evidence for account-to-payment reconciliation.

components.name: General Ledger Integration
components.description: Controlled posting boundary from product processing to the authoritative general ledger.
components.responsibility: Create traceable, idempotent posting instructions, capture acknowledgements and exceptions, and support reconciliation from source transaction to ledger entry.

components.name: Regulatory Reporting Integration
components.description: Governed extraction and delivery boundary for regulatory-reporting inputs.
components.responsibility: Produce lineage-bearing extracts from identified authoritative sources, validate completeness, record delivery evidence, and quarantine ambiguous or unreconciled outputs.

components.name: Migration Data Pipeline
components.description: Restartable pipeline for profiling, transforming, loading and validating migration data.
components.responsibility: Extract from approved sources, preserve lineage, apply versioned transformations, load idempotently, validate referential and product dependencies, and quarantine rejected records.

components.name: Reconciliation and Evidence Service
components.description: Cross-estate business and financial reconciliation capability.
components.responsibility: Compare counts, identities, balances, transactions, payment outcomes, ledger postings and reporting extracts; classify exceptions; and retain tamper-evident wave evidence.

components.name: Cutover and Recovery Orchestrator
components.description: Controlled execution engine for wave cutover, rollback and exception workflows.
components.responsibility: Execute approved runbooks, verify gates, quiesce affected scope, coordinate state changes and dependencies, stop on failed gates, and invoke rollback or forward-recovery workflows.

components.name: Batch and End-of-Day Controller
components.description: Dependency-aware control layer for legacy, target and transitional batch workloads.
components.responsibility: Maintain an evidenced dependency graph, coordinate scheduler execution, record checkpoints, prevent overlapping authoritative jobs, and support restart, hold and recovery decisions.

components.name: Cross-Estate Observability Service
components.description: Unified technical and business monitoring across coexistence.
components.responsibility: Correlate channel, routing, core, payment, batch, ledger, reporting and reconciliation telemetry; detect stale migration state and control failures; and support operational response.

components.name: Identity, Policy and Audit Controls
components.description: Shared security controls for human and service actions across both estates.
components.responsibility: Enforce authenticated identities, least privilege, segregation of duties, approval policy, secrets protection and immutable audit records for privileged and migration operations.

interfaces.name: Channel Capability API
interfaces.owner: Retail banking with SRE operational ownership
interfaces.contract: Versioned customer, account, payment and product operations with authenticated subject, governed scope, correlation identifier and idempotency key for state-changing requests.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Synchronous result when known; timeout or indeterminate outcome is returned explicitly and must be queried before retry. The facade does not silently switch cores after dispatch.

interfaces.name: Normalized Routing Contract
interfaces.owner: Migration office architecture with SRE operational ownership
interfaces.contract: Normalized operation containing account or product routing key, correlation identifier, idempotency key and requested capability.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: A request is accepted only with a single resolvable governed scope. Missing, stale or conflicting state fails closed to an exception path rather than broadcasting to both cores.

interfaces.name: Migration State Read and Transition API
interfaces.contract: Versioned state reads plus conditional state transitions carrying expected version, prerequisite evidence, approver identities and reason.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: State changes use compare-and-set semantics. Version conflict, unavailable state or failed prerequisite prevents transition and routing change; cached state cannot authorize a new transition.
securityControls: Encryption in transit and at rest

interfaces.name: Legacy Core Processing Contract
interfaces.contract: Normalized command or query mapped to legacy online interfaces with stable correlation and legacy transaction identifiers.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Only legacy-authoritative scopes are accepted. Timeout is treated as an uncertain outcome; status inquiry and reconciliation precede retry. Unsupported idempotency is compensated by duplicate detection and operator review.

interfaces.name: Target Core Processing Contract
interfaces.contract: Normalized command or query mapped to target-core capabilities with correlation, idempotency and authoritative-scope evidence.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Only target-authoritative scopes are accepted. Duplicate keys return the prior outcome where supported; indeterminate outcomes enter inquiry and reconciliation rather than cross-core retry.

interfaces.name: Payment Instruction and Outcome Contract
interfaces.contract: Payment instruction, stable end-to-end identity, status, settlement outcome and exception reason linked to the originating account transaction.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Submission is at-least-once only where protected by idempotency or duplicate detection. Unknown rail outcomes are held for inquiry and reconciliation; automatic cross-core resubmission is prohibited.

interfaces.name: General Ledger Posting Contract
interfaces.source: Legacy or target product processing through CMP-07
interfaces.contract: Balanced posting instruction with source transaction identity, account and product lineage, accounting date, posting identity and acknowledgement.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Postings are retried only with stable identities. Rejection or unknown acknowledgement is placed in an exception queue and reconciled; migration acceptance cannot rely solely on message delivery.
securityControls: Segregation of posting and exception approval

interfaces.name: Regulatory Extract Contract
interfaces.contract: Versioned extract with reporting period, authoritative-source declaration, record lineage, completeness controls and delivery evidence.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Incomplete, duplicated, ambiguous or unreconciled extracts are quarantined and escalated. Replacement delivery is versioned and does not erase prior evidence.
securityControls: Encryption in transit and at rest

interfaces.name: Migration Data Transfer Contract
interfaces.source: Legacy core and approved data sources through CMP-09
interfaces.contract: Versioned datasets and transformations for customer, account, product, balance and transaction data with source identifiers, cohort identity and lineage.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Loads are restartable and idempotent by dataset and record identity. Rejected or dependency-incomplete records are quarantined; no cohort advances while blocking exceptions remain unapproved.

interfaces.name: Reconciliation Evidence Feed
interfaces.source: Legacy core, Target core, Payments, General ledger and Regulatory reporting
interfaces.owner: Finance for financial controls and Migration office for wave controls
interfaces.contract: Correlated snapshots and events for records, balances, transactions, payment states, ledger postings and reporting outputs.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Late or missing evidence marks reconciliation incomplete rather than successful. Differences are classified, retained and routed to an owner; acceptance requires an approved disposition.

interfaces.name: Cutover Control Contract
interfaces.target: CMP-03, CMP-02, CMP-09, CMP-10 and CMP-12
interfaces.contract: Approved wave plan, dependency scope, gate results, execution command, checkpoint, operator action and recovery decision.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Commands are conditional on current state and evidence. A failed or timed-out gate stops progression; recovery resumes from a recorded checkpoint or invokes an approved rollback or forward-recovery plan.

interfaces.name: Batch Scheduling and Checkpoint Contract
interfaces.target: Legacy core, Target core, General ledger and reporting dependencies
interfaces.contract: Dependency-aware job request, authoritative scope, business date, checkpoint, completion status, restartability and downstream release status.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: A job cannot run concurrently against conflicting authoritative scopes. Failure holds dependent jobs; restart begins only from a verified checkpoint, otherwise an approved recovery runbook is required.

interfaces.name: Telemetry and Audit Feed
interfaces.source: CMP-01 through CMP-12 and both core estates
interfaces.owner: SRE for telemetry and Security for security audit
interfaces.contract: Correlated technical events, business control events, migration state versions, operator actions and reconciliation status with defined ownership and classification.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Telemetry loss raises a control alert and can block a cutover gate where evidence is required. Monitoring failure does not silently convert an unknown business outcome into success.

dataArchitecture: Define an explicit system-of-record matrix for Customer, Account, Product, Balance, Transaction, Ledger, Migration state and Reconciliation evidence for every transition state.
Use stable business and transaction identifiers across both cores, payments, ledger, reporting and reconciliation; retain source-system identifiers for lineage.
Model migration state as versioned, append-audited data with account or governed cohort scope, dependency references, current authority, prerequisites, approvals and exception status.

Proposed state progression is LEGACY_ACTIVE, PREPARED, SHADOW_VALIDATED, CUTOVER_QUIESCED, TARGET_ACTIVE, with EXCEPTION and governed recovery states. Exact names and legal transitions require approval.
Do not treat shadow data as authoritative. During coexistence, each governed scope has one authoritative transaction processor; copies are used only for validation until activation.
Migration datasets are immutable by version, transformation rules are version controlled, rejected records are quarantined, and reruns are idempotent by cohort, dataset and record identity.
Reconciliation evidence links source records, target records, balances, transactions, payment outcomes, ledger postings, regulatory extracts, rule version and approved disposition.
Retention periods, masking rules and permitted reconciliation tolerances remain unresolved and must be set by accountable data, security, finance and reporting owners.
securityArchitecture: Use distinct human and service identities across legacy, target and migration services; prohibit shared privileged identities where technically feasible.
Apply least privilege and segregate preparation, execution, approval, exception disposition and audit review for migration and financial controls.
Require authenticated and encrypted service communication, with isolated credentials and secrets rotation governed by Security.
Fail closed for ambiguous migration state, unauthorised transition, invalid approval, integrity failure or missing mandatory evidence.
Record tamper-evident audit events for routing decisions, migration-state changes, data transformations, privileged actions, postings, extract deliveries and reconciliation dispositions.
Minimise sensitive data in telemetry and reconciliation stores; restrict access by operational purpose and monitor access.
Threat-model cross-estate trust boundaries, adapters, migration data paths, operator interfaces and rollback procedures before each relevant implementation increment.
deploymentRuntime: Use a coexistence deployment in which the facade, router, control plane, adapters and control services are independently deployable from both cores.
Isolate production processing, migration execution and evidence workloads so migration load cannot silently consume all online or end-of-day capacity.
Deploy router and state-read capability without a single runtime failure point; actual topology and capacity require measured workload evidence.
Keep legacy and target adapters close to their respective trust and network boundaries while exposing only normalized contracts to shared services.
Use staged configuration release for routing rules, transformation rules and batch definitions, with version pinning and rollback of configuration independent of banking-state rollback.
Separate environments and credentials for rehearsal and production; production cutover uses the same versioned runbook proven in rehearsal, with environment-specific approvals.
No cloud, vendor product, database or messaging technology is selected because the scenario provides no platform constraints or evaluated options.
resilienceFailurePaths: Migration-state unavailable or stale: reject state-changing routing, preserve the last confirmed authoritative assignment for safe reads only where policy allows, alert Operations, and prohibit cutover progression.

Core timeout after dispatch: classify as indeterminate, query by stable transaction identity, reconcile before retry, and never submit the same business command to the other core as an availability fallback.

Dual-posting indication: stop affected cohort processing where safe, quarantine further postings, establish authoritative outcomes from core, payment and ledger evidence, then execute an approved correction plan.
Data divergence: block cohort advancement, retain both versions and lineage, classify transformation versus source defects, correct through a new controlled dataset version, and rerun reconciliation.
Failed cutover before irreversible actions: hold traffic, restore the previous authoritative state using conditional transition, verify legacy readiness and reconcile in-flight work before reopening.

Failed cutover after irreversible payment or ledger actions: do not assume state rollback is safe; use a governed forward-recovery or compensating-action plan approved by the accountable business and financial owners.

Batch overrun or failed checkpoint: hold dependent jobs and downstream release, resume from a verified checkpoint where supported, otherwise invoke the approved recovery sequence and reconcile the business date.

Regulatory extract incomplete or inconsistent: quarantine delivery, notify Regulatory reporting, regenerate a versioned extract from identified authoritative sources, and preserve both failure and replacement evidence.
Observability or audit-feed loss during a wave: treat required evidence as unavailable, stop further migration-state progression, restore evidence capture and reconcile the unobserved interval.
Security-control failure or unauthorised action: deny the transition, isolate affected credentials or service, preserve evidence, invoke incident handling and require reapproval before resumption.
observabilityOperations: Correlate customer request, routing decision, migration-state version, core transaction, payment instruction, ledger posting, batch run, reporting extract and reconciliation result.
Monitor channel success and latency, routing failures, state freshness, core and adapter health, indeterminate outcomes, duplicate detections, batch progress and evidence-feed completeness.
Publish business-control views for unreconciled balances and transactions, unmatched payments, rejected postings, incomplete extracts and migration exceptions by cohort.

Define transition service-level indicators for availability, latency, failed requests, indeterminate outcomes, cutover duration, recovery duration, batch completion and reconciliation completion; thresholds require stakeholder approval.
Provide role-specific runbooks and dashboards for Operations, Payments, Finance, Regulatory reporting, Security, SRE, Migration office and Customer support.
Use alert ownership and escalation paths that distinguish technical failure from financial, reporting, security and customer-impacting exceptions.
Conduct rehearsals for cutover, rollback, forward recovery, payment uncertainty, ledger rejection, batch restart, observability loss and control-plane failure before affected waves.
transitionArchitecture: State 0—Discovery and containment: inventory interfaces, products, data ownership, batch dependencies, controls, failure modes and current service indicators; add correlation and monitoring before changing authority.

State 1—Coexistence foundation: deploy stable facade, adapters, router in legacy-authoritative mode, control-plane state registry, audit controls and reconciliation feeds without moving transaction authority.

State 2—Prepared cohort: profile and copy dependency-complete customer and account cohorts, load target data, validate referential integrity and rehearse online, payment, ledger, reporting and batch paths.

State 3—Shadow validated: execute non-authoritative comparison where supported, reconcile expected outcomes, resolve blocking differences and obtain approvals. Shadow processing must not create duplicate external postings.

State 4—Cutover quiesced: stop or drain affected activity according to an approved runbook, complete in-flight and batch checkpoints, run final delta migration and reconciliation, and conditionally update authority.

State 5—Target active: route the cohort only to the target core, intensify technical and business observation, reconcile payments and ledger postings, and retain the legacy recovery capability for the approved observation period.

State 6—Accepted or recovered: accept the wave after service, reconciliation, reporting and control gates pass; otherwise enter exception, rollback where still safe, or approved forward recovery where irreversible actions prevent rollback.

Migration waves should begin with dependency-complete, operationally understood cohorts and expand only after evidence review. Exact cohort sequence cannot be selected without product and batch dependency data.
Legacy capability retirement occurs only after all dependent cohorts, batch jobs, reports, interfaces, evidence obligations and recovery requirements have approved dispositions.

decisions.title: Use stable capability contracts with governed coexistence routing
decisions.selectedOption: Place a channel facade and policy-enforced router before legacy and target adapters; channels do not select a core.
alternatives: Modify every channel to select the core
Expose legacy and target APIs independently
Replace all channel integrations during each migration wave
decisions.rationale: Central routing preserves channel access while enabling incremental migration under the no-big-bang constraint.
tradeoffs: Adds an online dependency and operational complexity
Requires normalized contracts and adapter maintenance
Reduces channel-specific migration logic and inconsistent routing
consequences: Router resilience and state consistency become critical.
Core-specific behavior must be made explicit in adapters.
Routing decisions require auditable correlation.

decisions.title: Make versioned migration state authoritative for routing
decisions.selectedOption: Use a dedicated control plane with conditional transitions, dependency gates, approvals and immutable state history.
alternatives: Infer state from target data presence
Maintain state separately in each channel
Use manual routing tables without workflow controls
decisions.rationale: Explicit governed state is required to route deterministically and support auditable coexistence.
tradeoffs: Introduces a high-value control dependency
Requires state governance and reconciliation with actual core authority
Enables controlled, explainable transitions
consequences: Ambiguous or stale state must fail closed.
State changes require segregation of duties and audit.
The registry must not become the balance or transaction system of record.

decisions.title: Enforce one authoritative transaction processor per governed scope
decisions.selectedOption: Assign each account or approved dependency cohort to exactly one authoritative core for state-changing processing at a time.
alternatives: Active-active writes to both cores
Best-effort broadcast with later deduplication
Core selection per individual transaction without governed state
decisions.rationale: Single authority limits dual posting and divergence while allowing non-authoritative shadow comparison.
tradeoffs: Cross-cohort transactions require explicit orchestration
Target activation may require quiescence
Avoids general distributed dual-write consistency
consequences: The scope boundary and cross-scope transaction behavior must be defined.
Shadow processing cannot emit external financial effects.
Unknown outcomes are reconciled rather than retried against the other core.

decisions.title: Migrate by dependency-complete waves
decisions.selectedOption: Plan account- or cohort-level waves only after customer, product, payment, batch, ledger and reporting dependencies are identified and gated.
alternatives: Migrate arbitrary account samples
Migrate one entire core at once
Move data independently of product and batch dependencies
decisions.rationale: The scenario prohibits a big bang and states that migration ordering is constrained by product dependencies.
tradeoffs: Discovery and wave planning take longer
Some products may remain in coexistence longer
Limits blast radius and supports evidence-based expansion
consequences: A dependency model and cohort eligibility rules are required.
Pilot selection cannot be finalized from the supplied evidence.
Wave acceptance becomes a governance decision based on recorded gates.

decisions.title: Use reconciliation as a mandatory migration gate
decisions.selectedOption: Reconcile data, balances, transactions, payments, ledger postings and reporting inputs before, during and after every wave.
alternatives: Validate record counts only
Reconcile only after cutover
Rely on technical success responses
decisions.rationale: Technical completion does not demonstrate financial or reporting correctness, and reconciliation is a critical requirement.
tradeoffs: Requires cross-system identifiers and retained evidence
May delay wave progression while exceptions are resolved
Provides a defensible basis for acceptance and recovery
consequences: Missing evidence is not considered success.
Tolerance and exception-approval policies must be defined by accountable owners.
Reconciliation services need read access without gaining transaction authority.

decisions.title: Implement state-machine cutover with rollback and forward recovery
decisions.selectedOption: Execute versioned runbooks through controlled checkpoints, allowing rollback only while its safety prerequisites remain true and otherwise using approved forward recovery.
alternatives: Manual cutover commands
Always roll back to legacy after failure
Continue automatically after failed gates
decisions.rationale: Payments, postings and other external effects may make a simple state reversal unsafe; recovery must account for irreversible outcomes.
tradeoffs: Requires detailed recovery analysis and rehearsals
Forward recovery can be operationally complex
Prevents unsafe assumptions of universal reversibility
consequences: Each wave must declare a rollback boundary and compensating actions.
Failed gates stop progression.
Consequential actions require segregated approval and complete audit.

decisions.title: Transition batch through an evidenced dependency controller
decisions.selectedOption: Inventory and control legacy, target and transitional jobs through dependency-aware scheduling, checkpoints and per-scope authority.
alternatives: Lift and shift all batch jobs unchanged
Rewrite all batch before online migration
Operate independent schedulers without cross-estate coordination
decisions.rationale: Incomplete batch documentation and end-of-day dependencies create material operational and data-integrity risk.
tradeoffs: Requires discovery and temporary cross-estate orchestration
May retain some legacy jobs longer
Provides controlled restart and downstream release
consequences: Unknown dependencies block affected wave readiness.
Conflicting authoritative jobs are prohibited.
Batch completion includes business reconciliation, not scheduler status alone.

decisions.title: Treat business observability and security controls as cutover prerequisites
decisions.selectedOption: Require correlated technical telemetry, business reconciliation, authenticated operations, segregation of duties and immutable audit evidence for migration progression.
alternatives: Monitor infrastructure only
Add audit and business controls after migration
Permit emergency unaudited state changes
decisions.rationale: Cross-estate health cannot be determined from infrastructure signals alone, and coexistence expands privileged control boundaries.
tradeoffs: Increases implementation and evidence effort
May block a wave when monitoring is incomplete
Improves detection, accountability and recovery confidence
consequences: Service-level thresholds and owners must be approved.
Loss of mandatory evidence blocks progression.
Operational tooling must restrict and audit privileged actions.

decisions.title: Preserve external integration contracts through controlled adapters
decisions.selectedOption: Use protocol-specific adapters with stable identities, explicit uncertain outcomes and idempotent or duplicate-detected delivery for payments, ledger and reporting.
alternatives: Directly couple both cores to every downstream system
Replace all downstream interfaces during core migration
Assume message delivery establishes business completion
decisions.rationale: Known integrations include APIs, payment rails, postings, files and extracts, while legacy documentation is incomplete.
tradeoffs: Adapters add temporary and possibly enduring components
Idempotency support varies by legacy interface
Limits downstream change and makes failure semantics explicit
consequences: Every integration requires contract discovery and testing.
Unknown outcomes require inquiry and reconciliation.
Adapter retirement depends on downstream migration evidence.

risks.description: Both cores or repeated integration delivery may create duplicate financial effects or dual posting.
risks.mitigation: Enforce one authoritative processor per scope, stable transaction and posting identities, duplicate detection, explicit uncertain-outcome handling, and cross-core/payment/ledger reconciliation.
risks.owner: Finance with Payments and Migration office

risks.description: Source, target, payment, ledger or reporting data may diverge during coexistence or migration.
risks.mitigation: Use lineage-bearing migration versions, controlled deltas, authority mapping, pre/during/post-wave reconciliation, quarantine and approved exception disposition.
risks.owner: Migration office with Finance and data owners

risks.description: A cutover may fail or leave routing authority inconsistent with actual processing state.
risks.mitigation: Use conditional state transitions, quiescence, checkpoints, gate evidence, rehearsed rollback and forward-recovery procedures, and state-to-core reconciliation.

risks.description: Batch overrun, hidden dependencies or unsafe restart may delay end-of-day processing or corrupt downstream outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Discover the dependency graph, establish checkpoints and restart semantics, prevent conflicting jobs, rehearse failure recovery, and hold downstream release until reconciliation completes.

risks.description: Incorrect source selection, posting divergence or incomplete extracts may cause regulatory misreporting or ledger inconsistency.
risks.mitigation: Maintain source-of-truth mapping, reconcile postings and extracts, version deliveries, preserve lineage, and require Finance and Regulatory reporting approval for exceptions.

risks.description: Routing, cutover or target-core failure may disrupt customer access or produce unresolved outcomes.

risks.owner: Retail banking with SRE and Customer support

risks.description: Incomplete legacy interface and batch documentation may conceal behavior or dependencies that invalidate a migration plan.
risks.mitigation: Instrument current flows, capture contracts and failure behavior, reconcile observed dependencies, run representative rehearsals and block affected cohorts until evidence is sufficient.

risks.description: Unavailable, stale or corrupted migration state may cause incorrect routing or prevent safe processing.

risks.description: Rollback may be unsafe after external payment, ledger or reporting effects become irreversible.
risks.mitigation: Declare per-wave rollback boundaries, track external effects, stop automatic reversal after the boundary, and rehearse authorised forward-recovery and compensating-action plans.
risks.owner: Risk with Payments, Finance and Migration office

risks.description: Expanded cross-estate privileges or inadequate segregation may permit unauthorised migration, posting or exception actions.
risks.mitigation: Use distinct identities, least privilege, multi-party approval, segregated roles, privileged-session controls, immutable audit and regular access review.
