delivery.executiveSummary: The candidate architecture introduces a stable channel facade, deterministic coexistence router and versioned migration control plane around legacy and target cores. Each governed account or dependency cohort has one authoritative transaction processor. Migration proceeds through evidence-gated waves with restartable data movement, business and financial reconciliation, dependency-aware batch control, and explicit cutover, rollback and forward-recovery paths. General-ledger and regulatory-reporting obligations remain external authoritative controls. Production acceptance is not claimed; service thresholds, source-of-truth ownership, dependency discovery, reconciliation tolerances and rollback boundaries require accountable approval.

sddSections.heading: Current-state diagnosis
sddSections.content: The estate contains legacy and target cores connected to channels, payments, customer information, product processors, the general ledger, batch scheduling and regulatory reporting. The main architectural hazards are incomplete interface and batch documentation, product-dependent migration ordering, dual posting, divergence, failed cutover, batch overrun, misreporting and customer disruption. Current quantitative service, volume and recovery evidence is not supplied.

sddSections.heading: Target architecture
sddSections.content: Channels use stable capability APIs. A governed router resolves versioned migration state and invokes one authoritative core through anti-corruption adapters. Payment, ledger and reporting integrations retain stable identities and explicit failure semantics. Migration data, reconciliation, cutover, batch, observability and identity services provide transition control without taking ownership of banking balances or ledger truth.

sddSections.heading: Transition states and waves
sddSections.content: Cohorts progress from legacy authority through preparation, shadow validation, quiesced cutover and target authority, with exception and recovery paths. Dependency completeness, data validation, service readiness, reconciliation, batch readiness, security controls and approvals gate every consequential transition.

sddSections.heading: Cutover and rollback
sddSections.content: Cutover uses versioned runbooks, quiescence, in-flight transaction handling, final data delta, reconciliation and conditional authority change. Rollback is allowed only before its declared safety boundary. After irreversible payment or ledger effects, the design uses approved forward recovery or compensating actions rather than assuming state reversal is safe.

sddSections.heading: Data and financial integrity
sddSections.content: Stable identities and lineage connect source and target data to transactions, payments, ledger postings, extracts and reconciliation evidence. Migration loads are versioned, restartable and idempotent. Missing evidence or unresolved blocking differences prevents wave acceptance.

sddSections.heading: Security and operations
sddSections.content: Cross-estate controls use authenticated identities, least privilege, segregation of duties, protected secrets, encrypted transport, tamper-evident audit and restricted exception handling. Unified technical and business observability supports SRE, Operations, Finance, Payments, Reporting, Security, Migration and Customer support.

sddSections.heading: Decision status
sddSections.content: All ADRs in this package are candidate decisions. No vendor, hosting platform, database, messaging product, numeric service target, reconciliation tolerance or regulatory interpretation has been selected.

openIssues: Approve the system-of-record matrix for every data domain and transition state.
Discover and approve legacy interface contracts, failure semantics and batch dependency graph.
Define migration cohort dependency and eligibility rules.
Define measurable transition service indicators, thresholds and observation periods.
Define reconciliation rules, permitted tolerances and exception authorities.
Identify irreversible payment, ledger and reporting actions and approve rollback boundaries.
Confirm target-core capability coverage for every product and customer journey.
Set data retention, masking, access and evidence requirements.
Assign named accountable owners and segregated approvers for production transitions.
Validate runtime topology and capacity using measured workload, data-volume and batch-window evidence.
implementationRoadmap: Foundation discovery: instrument current flows, inventory interfaces and batch dependencies, establish data ownership, baseline service indicators, and document failure semantics.
Control foundation: implement identities, audit, stable correlation, migration-state registry, approval workflow and read-only reconciliation collection.
Coexistence foundation: introduce facade, router and adapters in legacy-authoritative mode; prove that routing failure cannot cause cross-core duplicate execution.
Migration factory: implement versioned extraction, transformation, loading, quarantine, lineage and reconciliation for dependency-complete cohorts.
Operational foundation: implement cutover orchestration, batch checkpoints, dashboards, alerts, support procedures and rehearsed recovery runbooks.
Pilot wave: select a well-understood dependency-complete cohort, complete shadow validation, execute approved cutover, observe and reconcile before acceptance.
Controlled expansion: increase product and cohort coverage only after evidence review; migrate associated batch, ledger and reporting dependencies in each wave.
Retirement: remove legacy routes, jobs and adapters only after dependent capabilities, records, reports, evidence and recovery obligations have approved closure.
acceptanceAndFitnessTests: For every migration state, verify that the same governed scope resolves deterministically to one authoritative core and that missing, conflicting or stale state fails to the defined safe path.
Inject a core timeout after dispatch and verify that status inquiry and reconciliation occur before retry and that the request is not sent to the other core.
Submit duplicate payment and ledger identities and verify duplicate detection or idempotent outcome without an additional external financial effect.

For each rehearsal and production candidate wave, reconcile source and target records, balances, transactions, payment outcomes, ledger postings and regulatory extracts against approved rules and tolerances.
Attempt an unauthorised or unsegregated state transition and verify denial, alerting and immutable audit evidence.
Fail each cutover gate and verify progression stops at a recorded checkpoint with the approved rollback or forward-recovery path available.
Exercise a rollback before the declared safety boundary and verify restoration of authority, handling of in-flight work and post-recovery reconciliation.
Exercise a simulated failure after an irreversible external effect and verify that unsafe rollback is prevented and the approved forward-recovery workflow is invoked.
Interrupt migration data loading and verify restartability, stable record identity, quarantine behavior and retained lineage.
Fail or overrun a batch job and verify dependent jobs are held, restart occurs only from a verified checkpoint, and downstream release waits for reconciliation.
Remove mandatory telemetry during a rehearsal and verify that the control alert is raised and migration progression is blocked where evidence is required.
Run representative channel journeys during coexistence and compare approved service indicators with transition thresholds; no numeric threshold is asserted by this candidate.
Trace a sampled business transaction end to end through routing state, core outcome, payment or ledger effect, reporting input and reconciliation evidence.
Verify that sensitive data is minimized in telemetry, privileges are role-appropriate, credentials are isolated, and privileged actions are attributable.

abstentions: No quantitative availability, latency, recovery, batch-window or migration-duration guarantee is proposed because no measured baseline or approved target is supplied.
No specific regulatory obligation or retention period is inferred beyond the stated authority of general-ledger and regulatory-reporting obligations.
No vendor product, cloud model, database, event platform or implementation language is selected.
No migration cohort order is asserted without the missing product and batch dependency evidence.
No universal rollback guarantee is made after irreversible external financial effects.
No claim is made that legacy interfaces or batch dependencies are completely known.
unsupportedClaimsRejected: A zero-downtime or zero-disruption migration guarantee.
A single big-bang replacement of the legacy core.
Active-active financial writes to both cores without an established consistency and reconciliation design.
Automatic rollback after payment, ledger or reporting effects regardless of reversibility.
Technical message delivery as proof of financial or regulatory correctness.
Production approval, regulatory approval or stakeholder acceptance.
Any exact service-level number, reconciliation tolerance, data-retention period or batch capacity not present in the scenario.

problemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Deliver an enterprise agentic application that coordinates specialist capabilities and allowlisted tools while bounding autonomy, privilege, data access, failure propagation, latency and cost.
scope: Goal intake and governed task decomposition
Coordination of specialist capabilities
Model access through a controlled gateway
Policy-controlled tool invocation
Working and durable memory
Human approval and escalation
Audit, evaluation and operational observability
Failure containment and deployment boundaries
journeys: A user submits a goal; the orchestrator establishes identity and tenant context, creates a governed plan and delegates bounded tasks.
A specialist capability receives only task-scoped context and returns a typed proposal without receiving tool credentials or inherited privileges.
The orchestrator requests a deterministic policy decision for a proposed tool action; high-impact actions are held for explicit human approval.
The tool gateway validates the action, authorization permit and approval binding before invoking an allowlisted enterprise API.
Working memory supports the active run; policy-governed durable memory stores approved information under tenant, classification and retention controls.
Failures, ambiguity, exhausted budgets or uncertain external outcomes stop or suspend the run and route it to a human.
Plans, policy decisions, approvals, model interactions, tool calls and outcomes produce correlated audit and evaluation evidence.

qualityDrivers.statement: Treat prompts, retrieved data, model output and tool output as untrusted data and prevent them from changing policy or authority.
qualityDrivers.rationale: The scenario identifies prompt injection and untrusted retrieved or tool content as primary risks.

qualityDrivers.statement: Contain model, specialist and tool failures at explicit boundaries without transferring or expanding authority.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Models and tools may fail or become unavailable, and delegated execution must not create cascading authority.

qualityDrivers.statement: Enforce classification, least privilege and tenant isolation at identity, memory, model and tool boundaries.
qualityDrivers.rationale: The application processes enterprise data and must prevent privilege sharing and data leakage.

qualityDrivers.statement: Correlate quality, safety, latency, cost and policy telemetry across every run.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Agentic behavior requires end-to-end evidence for operations, evaluation and audit.

constraints: AA-C-001: No model or agent may directly mutate approved enterprise state.
AA-C-002: High-impact external actions require deterministic policy and explicit approval.
Models may fail, hallucinate or be unavailable.
Tool results and retrieved content are untrusted inputs.
Tools are assumed to expose bounded APIs and service identities.
A policy engine and approval service are assumed to be available.
assumptions: Enterprise identity can provide authenticated principal and tenant context.
Tool owners can define allowlisted operations, input schemas and impact classifications.
The policy engine can return an explicit allow, deny or approval-required decision with decision metadata.
The approval service can bind an approver decision to a specific proposed action.
Memory records can carry tenant, provenance, classification and retention metadata.
ambiguities: The taxonomy for high-impact actions is not supplied.
Tenant isolation requirements do not specify whether logical or physical isolation is required.
Data classification categories and permitted model destinations are not supplied.
Retention periods for working memory, durable memory, approvals and audit evidence are not supplied.
Tool APIs do not specify idempotency, transaction or reconciliation capabilities.
Run budget thresholds for steps, elapsed time, model usage and cost are not supplied.
The required degree of human review for durable-memory writes is not supplied.
unresolvedQuestions: Which actions and data combinations are classified as high impact?
Which approver roles and separation-of-duty rules apply to each action class?
Which tools support idempotency keys, status lookup, cancellation or compensating actions?
What data classifications may be sent to each model endpoint?
What are the tenant isolation and residency requirements?
What retention and deletion policies apply to memory and audit evidence?
Which operational thresholds stop a run or require escalation?
What evidence must be retained for model-risk and privacy review?

systemContext: End users interact through C-01 User Experience and API Boundary.
C-10 Identity and Tenant Context Adapter establishes principal, tenant and role context from the enterprise identity integration.
C-02 Governed Orchestrator coordinates plans but cannot directly mutate enterprise state.
C-03 Specialist Capability Runtime executes bounded reasoning tasks and returns proposals, not authoritative commands.
C-08 Model Gateway Adapter mediates model access and treats responses as untrusted.
C-04 Policy Decision Point and C-05 Approval Coordinator govern proposed actions.
C-06 Tool Gateway and Controlled Action Executor is the only application path to mutating enterprise tools.
C-07 Governed Memory Service manages working and durable memory.
C-09 Audit, Observability and Evaluation Plane records correlated evidence and evaluates runs.
Enterprise tools, identity, model services and observability backends remain external systems with explicit trust boundaries.

components.name: User Experience and API Boundary
components.description: Authenticated entry point for goals, plan review, approval status, escalation and result presentation.
components.responsibility: Validate request envelopes, preserve user and tenant context, display proposed versus completed actions and avoid presenting model proposals as confirmed outcomes.

components.name: Governed Orchestrator
components.description: Deterministic run controller surrounding probabilistic planning and specialist execution.
components.responsibility: Manage the run state machine, decompose goals into typed tasks, enforce dependency ordering and budgets, request policy and approval decisions, stop on ambiguity and prevent direct enterprise mutation.

components.name: Specialist Capability Runtime
components.description: Isolation boundary for specialist agents or non-agent capabilities.
components.responsibility: Execute task-scoped reasoning with explicitly supplied context; return schema-constrained proposals and evidence without receiving another specialist's privileges, tool credentials or unrestricted memory access.

components.name: Policy Decision Point
components.description: Deterministic authorization and action-classification control.
components.responsibility: Evaluate principal, tenant, purpose, data classification, tool, operation, parameters and run context; return allow, deny or approval-required without executing the action.

components.name: Approval Coordinator
components.description: Human-in-the-loop control for high-impact, ambiguous and failed actions.
components.responsibility: Create approval requests bound to an immutable action proposal, verify approver authority, record the decision and invalidate approval if the action or governing context changes.

components.name: Tool Gateway and Controlled Action Executor
components.description: Exclusive application boundary for allowlisted enterprise-tool access.
components.responsibility: Validate typed requests, permits and required approvals; obtain operation-scoped service identity; apply egress and secret controls; execute or query tool actions; and report confirmed, failed or indeterminate outcomes.

components.name: Governed Memory Service
components.description: Tenant-aware storage boundary for transient working memory and policy-controlled durable memory.
components.responsibility: Separate working from durable memory, validate provenance and classification, enforce tenant access and retention metadata, filter retrieval and prevent unapproved model output from becoming authoritative durable state.

components.name: Model Gateway Adapter
components.description: Controlled integration boundary for model inference.
components.responsibility: Select only policy-permitted model endpoints, apply data-handling controls, enforce request and response schemas, collect usage metadata and return model output as untrusted proposals.

components.name: Audit, Observability and Evaluation Plane
components.description: Cross-cutting evidence, telemetry and offline evaluation boundary.
components.responsibility: Record correlated plans, delegation, policy decisions, approvals, model and tool metadata, outcomes, safety events, latency and cost while applying access, integrity and sensitive-data controls.

components.name: Identity and Tenant Context Adapter
components.description: Boundary between enterprise identity and application authorization context.
components.responsibility: Validate identity assertions, derive tenant and role context and provide immutable principal context without exposing reusable credentials to models or specialists.

interfaces.name: Goal and Run API
interfaces.contract: Authenticated, tenant-bound goal, constraints and attachments enter as a versioned request; responses distinguish proposals, pending actions and confirmed outcomes.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Duplicate submissions use a caller-supplied request identity where available; invalid or unauthenticated requests are rejected. Interrupted runs remain suspended or failed rather than being reported as complete.

interfaces.name: Identity Context Resolution
interfaces.contract: Resolve an authenticated assertion into immutable principal, tenant and role context for the run.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Missing, expired, contradictory or unavailable identity context fails closed; no anonymous privilege substitution occurs.
securityControls: Audience and issuer checks as configured

interfaces.name: Model Inference Contract
interfaces.contract: Send a purpose-tagged, classification-aware request and receive a schema-constrained response plus model and usage metadata.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Malformed, policy-ineligible or incomplete output is rejected. Availability failures trigger only policy-permitted bounded retry or fallback; otherwise the task suspends, fails or escalates.

interfaces.name: Bounded Specialist Task Contract
interfaces.contract: Provide task identity, purpose, allowed context, expected output schema and run budget; receive a proposal with provenance and confidence or uncertainty indicators.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: A specialist cannot expand task scope or delegate authority. Timeout, invalid output or uncertainty returns control to the orchestrator without acquiring tool or memory privileges.

interfaces.name: Policy Decision Contract
interfaces.contract: Evaluate a normalized request containing principal, tenant, purpose, classification, resource, operation, parameter digest and run context; return allow, deny or approval-required with decision metadata.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Policy timeout, malformed response or unavailable policy fails closed for protected operations. A decision cannot authorize changed parameters or a different principal, tenant, purpose or operation.

interfaces.name: Approval Contract
interfaces.contract: Submit the human-readable action, normalized action digest, impact reason, policy decision and required approver role; receive approve, reject or pending.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Pending, unavailable or expired approval causes no execution. Any material proposal change invalidates the prior approval. Ambiguous approver identity or authority fails closed.
securityControls: Role and separation-of-duty evaluation as configured
No approval through model-generated identity claims

interfaces.name: Memory Access Contract
interfaces.contract: Read or write records using tenant, subject, purpose, classification, provenance, memory tier and retention metadata.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Cross-tenant, unclassified or policy-denied access is rejected. If required memory is unavailable, the task suspends or fails rather than silently using another tenant or stale unverified context.
securityControls: Encryption in transit and at rest

interfaces.name: Authorized Action Envelope
interfaces.contract: Submit a typed proposed action with tenant and principal context, purpose, policy decision, approval evidence when required, parameter digest and idempotency metadata where supported.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Missing, denied, mismatched or stale authorization is rejected. The gateway never interprets free-form model text as an executable action.

interfaces.name: Enterprise Tool Invocation
interfaces.contract: Invoke only the approved bounded API operation using an operation-scoped service identity and normalized parameters.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Safe automatic retry occurs only when the operation's idempotency semantics are known. Timeout or uncertain completion is marked indeterminate, checked through tool status or reconciliation where supported and otherwise escalated; success is never inferred from absence of error.

interfaces.name: Audit and Telemetry Event Contract
interfaces.contract: Emit correlated, versioned events for plans, delegation, policy, approvals, model use, memory access, tool calls, outcomes, failures, latency, safety and cost metadata.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Events use durable delivery and deduplication where implemented. If required audit evidence cannot be durably accepted, protected actions fail closed; other event handling follows an explicitly approved degradation policy and never silently discards evidence.

dataArchitecture: Represent each run with immutable identity, tenant, principal, purpose, status and correlation identifiers.
Version plans and tasks; retain the originating goal, constraints, dependencies, specialist proposals and deterministic controller decisions.
Use typed action proposals rather than executable free-form text. Bind policy and approval records to the normalized action and relevant context.
Separate ephemeral working memory from durable memory. Durable writes require explicit policy, provenance, classification, tenant and retention metadata.
Mark user input, retrieved content, model output and tool output as untrusted; preserve source provenance through planning and evaluation.
Store secrets outside prompts, plans, memory and audit payloads; components receive only references or scoped runtime credentials.
Record confirmed, failed and indeterminate tool outcomes distinctly to prevent uncertain effects from being treated as success.
Apply deletion and retention workflows independently to working memory, durable memory and audit evidence according to policies that remain to be defined.
securityArchitecture: Models and specialist capabilities are proposal producers, not security principals and not authoritative executors.
Establish principal and tenant context before planning; do not derive authority from prompt content or model output.
Use task-scoped capabilities so delegation carries only purpose, data and operations explicitly granted to that task.
Route every protected model, memory and tool request through deterministic policy enforcement.
Require explicit approval for policy-classified high-impact actions and bind that approval to the exact action proposal.
Make C-06 the exclusive enterprise-state mutation path; deny direct network or credential access from C-02, C-03 and models to enterprise tools.
Treat retrieved and tool content as data: delimit it from instructions, validate structured fields and prevent it from changing policies, scopes or system prompts.
Enforce tenant-aware authorization, classification checks, encrypted transport and storage, controlled egress, managed secrets and sensitive-data minimization.
Validate all model and tool outputs against typed schemas and business invariants before they influence subsequent actions.
Restrict access to audit and evaluation data because it can contain goals, prompts, tool parameters and outcomes.
deploymentRuntime: Deploy user ingress, orchestration, specialist runtime, model adapter, memory, tool execution and control-plane services as separate trust boundaries where the platform permits.
Deny direct enterprise-tool network paths from model-facing and specialist runtimes; permit tool egress only through C-06.
Use independently controlled service identities for orchestration, policy, approval, memory, model gateway, audit and each tool integration.
Persist run state around external calls so a process restart does not imply that an action failed or succeeded.
Use queues or durable work records for suspended approvals, bounded asynchronous tasks and audit delivery; preserve tenant and correlation context.
Scale model-facing and tool-facing workloads independently, subject to policy, quota and run budgets.
Deploy health checks and dependency isolation so model, tool, memory or audit degradation does not automatically expand privileges or bypass controls.
Keep production topology, isolation model, regions, capacity and recovery objectives unresolved until enterprise requirements are supplied.
resilienceFailurePaths: Prompt or retrieved-content injection: retain the content as untrusted data, reject attempts to alter authority, validate resulting proposals and raise a safety event when detected.
Malformed or hallucinatory model output: reject schema-invalid output; request constrained correction only within the run budget, otherwise fail or escalate.
Model unavailable: apply only policy-permitted bounded retry or fallback; otherwise suspend the task and present the failure to a human.
Specialist failure: contain the failure to its task, revoke task context and prevent delegation from acquiring broader authority.
Policy or identity unavailable: fail closed for protected operations and retain the run as suspended or failed.
Approval unavailable, rejected or stale: do not execute; retain pending or rejected state and notify the appropriate actor.
Memory unavailable: stop tasks that require memory correctness; never substitute unscoped, cross-tenant or unverified context.
Tool timeout or connection loss: classify the outcome as indeterminate, avoid blind retry, query status or reconcile where supported and escalate unresolved effects.
Partial tool failure: record completed and failed effects separately; use an approved compensating operation only when the tool owner defines one.
Audit delivery failure: require durable evidence before protected execution; otherwise follow an approved degradation policy without silent loss.
Runaway loop, latency or cost: the deterministic controller stops further model, specialist and tool calls when configured budgets are reached and escalates or returns a bounded partial result.
Evaluation detects unsafe or poor behavior: quarantine the affected workflow or model route through operational controls; no automatic promotion or authority expansion occurs.
observabilityOperations: Use a run correlation identifier across goal, plan, task, model, policy, approval, memory and tool events.
Expose run state, pending approvals, blocked actions, retries, indeterminate tool effects and final disposition.
Measure model and specialist failures, schema rejection, policy deny and approval-required outcomes, tool errors, memory access denials and injection detections.
Collect latency and cost metadata by run, task, specialist, model and tool without inventing target thresholds.
Alert on repeated authorization failures, cross-tenant access attempts, runaway-loop stops, audit delivery failures and unresolved tool outcomes.
Evaluate representative workflows offline for task quality, unsafe instruction following, privilege escalation, data leakage and tool misuse before production acceptance.
Use access-controlled replay based on minimized evidence; do not replay mutating actions against production tools.
Define operational ownership and runbooks for model outage, policy outage, approval backlog, memory failure, tool indeterminacy and audit degradation.
transitionArchitecture: Phase 1: Define action-impact taxonomy, tenant model, data classifications, tool contracts, approval roles, retention rules and run budgets.
Phase 2: Implement identity context, deterministic run state machine, typed plans and model output validation with no mutating tools enabled.
Phase 3: Add isolated specialists and governed working memory; validate privilege separation and prompt-injection controls.
Phase 4: Integrate policy, approval and a non-mutating or test tool through C-06; verify propose-authorize-execute semantics and audit evidence.
Phase 5: Add durable memory and selected mutating tools only after tool-specific idempotency, reconciliation, permissions and failure paths are accepted by their owners.
Phase 6: Operationalize evaluation, safety monitoring, cost controls, incident runbooks and controlled rollout.
Production acceptance remains an external governance decision and is not granted by this candidate architecture.

decisions.title: Use a deterministic run controller around probabilistic planning
decisions.selectedOption: A stateful governed orchestrator owns run transitions, budgets and escalation while models and specialists produce proposals.
alternatives: Allow a model-driven agent to control the loop directly
Use a fixed workflow with no dynamic decomposition
decisions.rationale: This supports dynamic task decomposition while ensuring that models cannot define their own authority or bypass deterministic controls.
tradeoffs: Adds controller and state-machine complexity
Constrains some open-ended agent behavior
Provides stronger replay, containment and auditability
consequences: Every external action is represented as an explicit run transition.
Unknown or invalid transitions fail closed.
Run budgets and escalation are enforced outside model reasoning.

decisions.title: Delegate capability without sharing privilege
decisions.selectedOption: Give specialists task-scoped context and require all privileged operations to pass through common policy, memory and tool boundaries.
alternatives: Give each specialist the orchestrator's credentials
Issue broad persistent credentials to each specialist
Run all specialist logic in one unrestricted agent
decisions.rationale: Task-scoped delegation prevents implicit privilege inheritance and limits failure propagation.
tradeoffs: Requires explicit context and capability design
May add policy calls and integration latency
Reduces specialist autonomy to bounded proposals
consequences: Specialists cannot call enterprise tools directly.
Privileges are evaluated against the originating principal, tenant, purpose and task.
Specialist compromise does not automatically confer another specialist's access.

decisions.title: Separate propose, authorize, approve and execute
decisions.selectedOption: Use typed action proposals, deterministic policy, action-bound approval and an exclusive controlled executor.
alternatives: Allow the orchestrator or model to invoke tools directly
Rely on prompt instructions to request approval
Approve an entire run without binding approval to actions
decisions.rationale: The separation enforces the prohibition on direct mutation and prevents model output from acting as authorization.
tradeoffs: Introduces additional states and user waiting time
Requires canonical action binding and tool schemas
Supports explicit control and forensic evidence
consequences: Changed parameters require a new decision and, when applicable, new approval.
High-impact execution cannot proceed while approval is pending or unavailable.
C-06 becomes the enforceable mutation boundary.

decisions.title: Separate working and durable memory
decisions.selectedOption: Use tenant-scoped ephemeral working memory and separately governed durable memory with explicit provenance, classification and retention metadata.
alternatives: Use one unrestricted shared memory store
Keep all context only in prompts
Persist all model output automatically
decisions.rationale: Different persistence and authority needs require different controls, and model output must not become durable enterprise knowledge by default.
tradeoffs: Adds lifecycle and synchronization complexity
May reduce recall when retention or classification blocks data
Improves deletion, access and provenance control
consequences: Durable writes pass through policy.
Retrieved memory remains untrusted input.
Cross-tenant access is denied at the memory boundary.

decisions.title: Use correlated durable audit evidence
decisions.selectedOption: Emit versioned, access-controlled audit events with integrity metadata and durable delivery for consequential transitions.
alternatives: Rely only on application logs
Store only final answers
Let each specialist retain independent uncorrelated logs
decisions.rationale: Plans, delegation, approvals and external effects must be reconstructable across service boundaries.
tradeoffs: Consumes storage and operational capacity
Requires sensitive-data minimization and retention governance
Enables evaluation, incident response and audit reconstruction
consequences: Protected execution depends on required evidence being durably accepted.
Audit access is separately controlled.
Evidence records distinguish proposals from confirmed effects.

decisions.title: Treat all non-deterministic and external content as untrusted
decisions.selectedOption: Delimit untrusted content, retain provenance, validate typed outputs and prevent content from modifying authority or control instructions.
alternatives: Trust retrieved enterprise content
Execute free-form model tool instructions
Sanitize only the initial user prompt
decisions.rationale: Injection can enter through users, memory, retrieval, model responses or tool outputs.
tradeoffs: Structured contracts may limit expressiveness
Validation can reject otherwise useful output
Reduces instruction-data confusion and unsafe execution
consequences: Free-form content is never directly executable.
Every boundary validates structure and permitted use.
Injection detections become safety and evaluation evidence.

decisions.title: Bound every run with deterministic budgets
decisions.selectedOption: Enforce configurable limits for steps, elapsed time, retries, model usage, tool calls and cost outside model control.
alternatives: Allow agents to decide when to stop
Use only model-provider quotas
Apply one global timeout without task state
decisions.rationale: External limits contain loops, latency and cost when model behavior is faulty or ambiguous.
tradeoffs: May stop legitimate complex tasks
Thresholds require operational tuning
Provides predictable containment and explicit escalation
consequences: Budget exhaustion causes a stopped or escalated state, not additional autonomous calls.
The audit plane records budget consumption and stop reasons.
Threshold values remain governance configuration rather than model instructions.

risks.description: Prompt injection through user, retrieved, memory or tool content influences plans or attempts to override controls.
risks.mitigation: Separate instructions from data, preserve provenance, validate typed proposals, deny authority changes from content and continuously evaluate injection scenarios.

risks.description: Excessive agency or tool misuse causes unauthorized or high-impact actions.
risks.mitigation: Use task-scoped delegation, deterministic policy, action-bound approval, exclusive controlled execution and deny direct model or specialist tool access.

risks.description: Data crosses tenant, classification, model or tool boundaries without authorization.
risks.mitigation: Bind tenant and classification context at ingress, enforce least privilege at every boundary, minimize prompt data, isolate memory and restrict model and tool routing.

risks.description: Agent loops or repeated calls produce uncontrolled latency or cost.
risks.mitigation: Enforce deterministic run budgets, bounded retry, concurrency and quota controls; stop and escalate when configured limits are reached.

risks.description: Tool timeout or partial completion creates duplicate, inconsistent or unknown enterprise effects.
risks.mitigation: Use idempotency where supported, persist action state, avoid blind retries, query tool status, distinguish indeterminate outcomes and require reconciliation or human handling.

risks.description: Delegation, approvals or tool outcomes cannot be reconstructed, resulting in unauditable behavior.
risks.mitigation: Use correlated durable events, action and decision binding, integrity metadata, controlled access and fail-closed evidence handling for protected actions.

risks.description: Model, specialist, policy, memory or tool failure cascades into repeated calls, unsafe fallback or incorrect success reporting.
risks.mitigation: Apply dependency-specific circuit breaking and bounded retries, persist run states, fail closed for authorization dependencies and escalate uncertain outcomes without authority expansion.

delivery.executiveSummary: The candidate architecture places a deterministic run controller around probabilistic models and specialist capabilities. Specialists receive task-scoped context but no inherited credentials. All consequential actions follow propose-policy-approve-execute semantics, with the tool gateway as the exclusive enterprise mutation path. Working and durable memory are separated by tenant, classification, provenance and retention controls. Correlated audit and evaluation evidence covers plans, delegation, policy, approval, model use, memory and tool outcomes. Production acceptance remains false because impact taxonomy, retention, tenant isolation, tool semantics, run thresholds and operating objectives are unresolved.

sddSections.heading: Architecture style
sddSections.content: A stateful governed orchestration architecture separates probabilistic proposal generation from deterministic authority, approval and execution.

sddSections.heading: Agent boundaries
sddSections.content: The orchestrator owns run state; specialists own bounded reasoning tasks; neither models nor specialists hold enterprise-tool credentials or directly mutate approved state.

sddSections.heading: Control plane
sddSections.content: Identity, policy, approval, budgets and audit form the control plane. Authorization is bound to principal, tenant, purpose, operation and exact action parameters.

sddSections.heading: Tool execution
sddSections.content: C-06 validates typed actions and authorization, then uses operation-scoped service identities. Unknown outcomes are reconciled or escalated rather than retried blindly.

sddSections.heading: Memory
sddSections.content: Working memory is scoped to the active run. Durable memory requires explicit policy and metadata for tenant, provenance, classification and retention; retrieval remains untrusted.

sddSections.heading: Security
sddSections.content: The design uses least privilege, task-scoped delegation, tenant enforcement, controlled egress, managed secrets, schema validation and injection-resistant instruction-data separation.

sddSections.heading: Operations and evaluation
sddSections.content: Correlated evidence supports run monitoring, incident response and offline evaluation of quality, safety, latency, cost and policy behavior.

sddSections.heading: Delivery status
sddSections.content: This is a candidate design only. Production acceptance depends on resolving open governance and operational requirements and passing the stated fitness tests.

openIssues: Define high-impact action classes and deterministic policy rules.
Define approver roles, separation of duty and approval validity rules.
Define tenant isolation, residency and data-classification requirements.
Define retention and deletion rules for each memory and evidence class.
Document idempotency, status-query and compensation semantics for each tool operation.
Set run, retry, latency, cost and quota thresholds through governance.
Define model endpoint eligibility and data-handling rules.
Define availability, recovery and evidence-retention objectives.
Define the approved degradation policy for audit and observability dependencies.
implementationRoadmap: Establish governance inputs: action taxonomy, data classifications, tenant model, tool inventory, approval roles and retention.
Build identity context, typed goal and plan contracts, deterministic run states and model output validation.
Introduce isolated specialist execution with task-scoped context and no tool connectivity.
Implement policy integration, action-bound approval and the exclusive tool gateway using non-mutating test operations first.
Add working memory, then durable memory after access and retention rules are defined.
Integrate tools incrementally after each tool owner supplies schemas, least-privilege scopes and failure semantics.
Implement correlated audit, operational dashboards, evaluation suites and incident runbooks.
Perform controlled rollout only after fitness tests and external production-acceptance governance complete.
acceptanceAndFitnessTests: Submit injected instructions through user, retrieved, memory and tool content; verify they cannot alter policy, system authority, tool allowlists or tenant context.
Attempt to use one specialist's task or privilege context from another specialist; verify denial and an auditable event.
Attempt direct enterprise mutation from a model, specialist or orchestrator; verify network, credential and application controls block it.
Propose a high-impact action without approval; verify no tool execution occurs.
Approve an action and then change its parameters, principal, tenant or purpose; verify the approval is invalidated.
Attempt cross-tenant memory read and durable write; verify denial without data disclosure.
Return malformed or adversarial model output; verify schema rejection and bounded failure handling.
Simulate model, policy, approval and memory outages; verify protected operations fail closed without authority expansion.
Simulate a tool timeout after possible completion; verify the outcome becomes indeterminate and no blind retry occurs.
Exhaust configured step, retry, time, tool-call or cost budgets; verify the run stops and escalates without further autonomous calls.
Interrupt the orchestrator around an external call; verify recovery preserves pending, confirmed and indeterminate action states.
Disrupt audit delivery before a protected action; verify execution follows the approved fail-closed evidence policy.
Verify audit reconstruction links goal, plan, specialist delegation, policy decision, approval, model usage, tool call and final outcome.
Verify durable-memory retention and deletion behavior after governance values are configured.
Run offline evaluations for injection resistance, privilege escalation, data leakage, tool misuse, task quality and false success reporting.

abstentions: No vendor, product, model or deployment platform is selected.
No numeric availability, latency, throughput, cost, recovery, retention or quality guarantee is asserted.
No regulatory or jurisdiction-specific obligation is inferred.
No physical tenant-isolation topology is selected without requirements.
No production approval, risk acceptance or control certification is granted.
unsupportedClaimsRejected: The scenario does not establish that any current implementation satisfies the requirements.
The scenario does not establish that a particular model is safe, accurate or available enough for production.
The scenario does not supply quantitative service objectives or run-budget thresholds.
The scenario does not establish tool idempotency, transactionality or compensation support.
The scenario does not supply approved retention periods, data classifications or high-impact action definitions.
